$comment: The conformance suites, declared once. `generate_ci.py` emits the oracle jobs of
.github/workflows/ci.yml from this file, and `run_suite.py` runs the same steps locally.
Same shape as picard-rs and htsjdk-rs; see picard-rs decision 0008 for why a golden that no
CI step re-derives is not evidence.

ci.$why: Suites share a job because each job restores the oracle image once.

suites.title: OriginalAlignment and the OA tag
suites.why: OriginalAlignment counts the reads supporting the best alternate allele whose original alignment was on a different contig, which is how a Mutect2 call on the mitochondrion is checked against a NuMT, and four of its decisions live outside the class. The allele it counts for is picked by TLOD through getTumorLogOdds and maxElementIndex, so a tie goes to the earliest alternate and a TLOD of dot is not missing but -1, which after the log conversion is an ordinary number that can win the maximum. The contig comparison is a string field: getOAContig splits the OA tag on a comma and takes field zero, so an unmapped read, whose tag is star comma zero and so on, has original contig star, which differs from every real contig and therefore counts. The filter takes BestAllele.isInformative, which compares against the log10 threshold whatever base the matrix is in. And unlike Coverage, MappingQualityZero and CountNs, which treat null likelihoods as nothing to say, this one calls Utils.nonNull and throws.

suites.title: MBQ, MMQ, MPOS and MFRL
suites.why: The four PerAlleleAnnotation members share one parent and disagree about everything the parent leaves open. An allele no read supports is annotated 0 by BaseQuality, 60 by MappingQuality, 50 by ReadPosition and 0 by FragmentLength, and the two invented values say why in a comment: an allele with no reads should not prejudice a site. Three filters run before a read contributes and they are not the same filter, so MappingQuality never sees a read of quality zero and its median can only be zero by way of the empty case, which is sixty. The value under the key is a Java int array, so it prints through Arrays.toString and carries the class [I rather than a list class. And includeRefAllele is false in the parent and overridden to true in three of the four, so MPOS reports one number per alternate allele where the others report one per allele including the reference. The median itself is commons-math3 Percentile finished with FastMath.round, which is floor(x + 0.5) and not Math.round; both are in jmath and this reaches the first.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner. The golden corrected the port on one point, and it is the shape of the data structure rather than the arithmetic: the buckets are keyed by the matrix's alleles while the loop runs over the variant's, so a variant allele the matrix never held looks up null and aggregate dereferences it. The port had it as an empty list, which would have produced the annotation's value for no reads, a plausible number where the reference produces no record at all.

suites.title: An INFO attribute as a double array
suites.why: Everything that reads a numeric annotation off a VariantContext goes through VariantContextGetters.attributeValueToDoubleArray, and the function is held together by an accident. Its Iterable branch tests value.getClass().isAssignableFrom(Iterable.class), which is backwards: isAssignableFrom asks whether the argument's type can be assigned to the receiver's, so it asks whether an Iterable fits in an ArrayList variable, which is false. Every list therefore falls through to the branch labelled as a last resort, which renders the value with String.valueOf and splits the result on a comma; String.valueOf of a list is bracketed and comma-space separated, so every field after the first arrives with a leading space and parses only because Double.parseDouble trims. A port splitting on comma-space, or using a parser that refuses leading whitespace, agrees on a one-element list and diverges on every longer one. Two more things the signature hides: a field equal to the missing value becomes the caller's missingValue, which is -1 for the overload every annotator uses, so a missing TLOD arrives as a number nobody can recognise as missing; and any other unparsable field becomes a GATKException naming the annotation rather than a NumberFormatException. The doubles travel as raw bits because getTumorLogOdds multiplies them by Math.log(10).

suites.title: The annotations that read the likelihood matrix
suites.why: Coverage, MappingQualityZero and CountNs are the three annotations whose whole input is the likelihood matrix. Their arithmetic is three counts and no two of the three agree on anything else. Only Coverage tests evidenceCount, so an empty matrix makes it write nothing while the other two write a zero. Only MappingQualityZero tests the site, so a non-variant site makes it write nothing while the other two still count. Coverage and MappingQualityZero go through String.format so their values are Strings, while CountNs puts a long into an ImmutableMap so its value is a Long: all three render identically and are three different objects to a consumer. And CountNs compares against the byte N, upper case only, reaching the base through getReadBaseAtReferenceCoordinate, whose bounds test uses the alignment span while its index uses the soft start, so a read whose N sits inside a soft clip does not count.

suites.title: The likelihood matrix and the best-allele search
suites.why: Every likelihood-reading annotation goes through searchBestAllele, and four of its decisions are invisible in its signature. bestAlleleIndex and secondBestIndex both start at zero and nothing means no second best, so a one-allele matrix ends with the two equal and the tail turns that into a second-best likelihood of negative infinity. The comparison is strictly greater, so among equal likelihoods the earliest allele wins and the allele order is observable in a result that looks order-independent. isInformative compares the confidence against LOG_10_INFORMATIVE_THRESHOLD whatever base the matrix is in, while the tie-breaking pass inside searchBestAllele converts its threshold with the base, so after switchToNaturalLog the two ask their question at different thresholds. And confidence is guarded by likelihood == secondBestLikelihood ? 0 : the difference, whose load-bearing case is the pair of negative infinities where the subtraction would be NaN. The likelihoods travel as raw bits because they are read back out of the matrix after a conversion.

suites.title: The allele and sample axes
suites.why: AlleleLikelihoods is defined over an AlleleList and a SampleList, so anything surprising about those two is inherited by every likelihood GATK computes. An indexed list is a set: IndexedSet drops a duplicate silently and the survivor keeps the index of its first occurrence, so a list built from A, C, A has two entries and nothing says so, and a caller that built its list from a variant context with a repeated allele gets a matrix with fewer rows than it asked for. Membership is Allele.equals, which is bases and the reference flag, so the reference A and a non-reference A are two entries in one list and indexOfReference reports only the first entry whose flag is set. And a permutation is a directional subset map: it may drop and reorder, never invent, refusing a longer target and a target holding an unknown allele with the same message both ways, while reporting isPartial, isNonPermuted and isKept, which callers use to skip work. A subset that keeps its order is partial and NOT non-permuted, which is the distinction a port collapses by accident.

suites.title: The counting INFO annotations
suites.why: ChromosomeCounts, SampleList and RawGtCount are the members of the counting family that need no AlleleLikelihoods, so they can be asked through their own interface. What is measured is not only the numbers but the shape of what an annotation returns, which is where a port goes wrong silently. The map is Map<String,Object>, so the Java class of each value is part of the answer: ChromosomeCounts puts an Integer for one alternate allele and an ArrayList for two or more, and both render the same way. An empty map is not zeroes, it means the keys are absent from the record, and each annotation has at least one guard reaching that branch. RawGtCount.annotate returns null rather than an empty map, a third thing again, and its real work is combineRawData, whose output drops one of the three counts it just summed and writes a literal dot in its place, so the result of a combine cannot be fed back into one. And SampleList's guard is isMonomorphicInSamples, which is not every genotype is hom-ref: a site with alternate alleles and no genotypes at all is not monomorphic, while a site where everybody is a no-call is.

suites.title: ReadFilterLibrary decisions
suites.why: One row per filter, one character per record: the reference's own decision, taken through SAMRecordToGATKReadAdapter rather than off the flags. Going through the adapter is the point: GATKRead.isUnmapped is three criteria and isFirstOfPair requires pairing, so comparing against flags would compare against a reimplementation of the adapter instead of the reference. The corpus travels in the same file as SAM text, so the port judges the records the reference judged rather than a description of them.
suites.$compare_why: Line mode, not keyed. Keyed compares one row per (kind, case) pair, and every dump here repeats a kind across many cases: the ReadClipper golden has 2,385 rows and only 181 distinct keys, so keyed mode silently compared 8% of it and reported ok. The whole file is the artefact and its order is part of it.

cases.why: ReadUtils maps a reference position to a read offset, and every walker, annotation and clipping operation stands on that arithmetic. It is probed from three bases before each read to three past it, so the not-found answers at both edges are measured rather than assumed.

Every cigar ReadClipper produces goes through CigarUtils.clipCigar and CigarBuilder, and the builder rewrites what it is handed: it merges, drops zero-length elements, removes deletions that land at either end, and moves a deletion that arrives after an insertion in front of it. Each rewrite is a byte difference in the output BAM of every clipping tool.

Clipping rewrites the read: bases, qualities, cigar, alignment start and, for a flow read group, some of its tags. The golden carries the whole clipped read for every entry point, because comparing one field would hide the others.

The bases a tool sees are not the bytes in the FASTA: CachingIndexedFastaSequenceFile upper-cases every query and flattens every IUPAC code to N. The fixture travels in the golden so the port reads the bytes the reference read, and the comparison covers the transformation rather than the file format.

CountingReadFilter's summary text is output a tool prints, so it is compared as bytes. It is also the only place the order of a conjunction is observable: the boolean cannot say which of WellformedReadFilter's eight filters rejected a read, and the counts can.

suites.title: ReadsDataSource interval queries
suites.why: Which reads a walker sees for a given -L is decided by htsjdk's stateful query filter, not by an overlap test: its interval index only advances and the traversal stops once every interval is behind the record, unmapped reads carrying their mate's position are special-cased, and QueryInterval.optimizeIntervals merges abutting intervals so two adjacent -L arguments return a spanning read once. The fixture BAM and its .bai travel in the golden as base64, so the port queries the bytes the reference queried.

cases.why: Produced by the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner and downloaded from that run's artifact, which is the only provenance this programme accepts for a golden. Three of its answers are worth naming: a query at 500-500 does not return the mapped read that starts at 500 with an empty cigar, because its alignment end is 499; a query at 495-505 does; and 499-499 stops the traversal outright.

suites.title: ReferenceContext windows
suites.why: A walker never queries the reference directly: it is handed a window around its position, and three of that window's behaviours are decisions. Near a contig edge the window is silently smaller than requested and numWindowLeadingBases reports what was obtained rather than what was asked for; getBases(leading, trailing) expands the window rather than the interval, so the expansions compose; and getKmerAround returns null rather than a shorter kmer when the edge prevents expansion. Each accessor gets its own row, so which call throws is measured rather than collapsed into one E.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner. Its sharpest row is the asymmetry between the two ways of asking for the same window: setWindow(3, 3) at chr1:1-1 crops silently to chr1:1-4, while the same window given as coordinates throws, because building SimpleInterval(chr1, -2, 4) is itself the error.

suites.title: What a ReferenceWalker traverses, and what CountBasesInReference counts
suites.why: The first member of the reference-utility archetype. AN ABSENT -L IS THE WHOLE REFERENCE, one apply per base of every contig in the sequence dictionary, which is a branch IntervalWalker cannot reach because its requiresIntervals() is true and Barclay rejects the run first. -XL ALONE IS THEREFORE LEGAL here and subtracts from that list. THE INTERVALS ARE SORTED INTO DICTIONARY ORDER rather than kept in the order given. EVERY LOCUS IS ONE BASE, IntervalLocusIterator at size one, so an eleven-base interval is eleven apply calls. THE BASE IS THE CACHING READER'S, not the file's: lower case comes back upper-cased and every IUPAC code comes back as N, which is what makes CountBasesInReference count five symbols rather than fifteen. AND getReferenceWindow IS A METHOD rather than an argument, so a walker that widens it sees more bases per locus while still being called once per base, clipped at the contig ends.

cases.why: 192 rows, no files that travel beyond the FASTA the harness writes: ten traversals of a two-contig reference built awkward on purpose -- mixed case, a line width that does not divide the length, an N run and IUPAC codes -- and three runs of CountBasesInReference over it. The traversals cover an absent -L, an interval, a whole contig, two intervals given out of dictionary order, an exclusion with no inclusion, padding, two abutting intervals, an interval past the end of its contig, and a walker that widens its own window. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32221539233, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: CountReads and CountBases, and what the engine does before apply
suites.why: The two smallest tools in GATK, and the second and third members of the reference-and-coverage archetype: their whole implementation is an apply that increments a counter, so what is measured is everything the engine does before apply is reached. THE DEFAULT FILTERS ARE NOT NOTHING: WellformedReadFilter runs on every read walker, so the read with no read group and the read with an N operator never reach apply. COUNTBASES COUNTS getLength(), the sequence, NOT THE SPAN, so a read with a ten-base deletion contributes ten and not twenty. -L RESTRICTS BOTH, and an unmapped read parked at its mate's coordinate is inside the interval while an unplaced read is outside every one. AN ADDED --read-filter IS ADDITIONAL rather than a replacement, and --disable-tool-default-read-filters is what counts the records the file actually holds. AND THE TWO TOOLS SEE THE SAME READS, which is what makes them one archetype.

cases.why: 21 rows, no files that travel: two BAMs the harness builds, the shared eleven-record fixture and a second one whose reads are fifteen, five, ten and zero bases long. Eight runs of each tool over the first -- everything, with a reference, each contig, the deletion window, a duplicate filter added, every default filter disabled, and an unknown contig -- and two over the second. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32269884234, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: A reference written out of a reference
suites.why: The fourth member of the reference archetype and the first that WRITES a reference. THE OUTPUT SEQUENCES ARE NUMBERED rather than named after the contig they came from: the name is a counter starting at one and the contig and coordinates go in the description. A GAP STARTS A NEW SEQUENCE, the test being withinDistanceOf(interval, 1), so two abutting intervals are one output sequence and two a base apart are two. CROSSING A CONTIG IS A GAP TOO, so a run with no -L over a two-contig reference writes two sequences. THE DESCRIPTION'S START IS THE SEQUENCE'S FIRST BASE and its end the last position seen, so it is the span written rather than the interval asked for. THE BASES ARE THE CACHING READER'S, so a FASTA written by this tool is not the FASTA it read: lower case comes back upper-cased and IUPAC codes come back as N. AND --line-width IS PER RUN, recorded in every index row.

cases.why: 29 rows, no files that travel: ten runs of the tool over the two-contig FASTA the harness writes, each printing the FASTA it produced with its .fai and its .dict. The runs cover no intervals at all, one interval, two intervals a base apart, two that abut, one per contig, the soft-masked stretch, the IUPAC stretch, a narrow line width, a line width of zero and a single base. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32277976227, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: A reference shifted, and the three files beside it
suites.why: The fifth member of the reference archetype and the first that needs nothing new. THE DEFAULT OFFSET IS HALF THE CONTIG by integer division, computed per contig. THE SHIFTED SEQUENCE IS THE TWO HALVES SWAPPED, tail first, written as two appendBases calls so the line break does not fall at the join. A CONTIG WHOSE OFFSET IS 0 OR THE WHOLE LENGTH IS SKIPPED ENTIRELY rather than copied unshifted, so it is absent from the output FASTA and from the chain file. THE CHAIN FILE IS TWO RECORDS PER CONTIG with an id that counts across contigs, the first record's score being the shift-back offset and the second's the offset minus one. THE INTERVAL FILES DIFFER BY THE CONTIG'S PARITY: the shifted end gains contigLength % 2 and the unshifted one does not, and both starts are shiftOffset/2, which is zero for a contig shifted by one. AND AN OFFSET LIST OF THE WRONG LENGTH IS A UserException.BadInput checked before any contig is written.

cases.why: 38 rows, no files that travel: seven runs over the two-contig FASTA the harness writes, each printing the shifted FASTA, its .fai, its .dict, the shift-back chain file and the two interval files. The runs cover the default half-length offsets, an explicit offset per contig, an offset of zero and an offset of the whole length (both skipped), a shift of one, a narrow line width and an offset list of the wrong size. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32282575530, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: A reference with a VCF applied to it
suites.why: FastaReferenceMaker with a VCF applied, so every base of the traversal is copied, replaced, dropped or expanded. A DELETION KEEPS ITS FIRST BASE AND DROPS THE NEXT n through a counter that survives from one apply to the next, so the bases removed are the ones after the record's position. AN INSERTION EMITS THE WHOLE ALTERNATE ALLELE, anchor base included, so one locus contributes several bases. A FILTERED RECORD IS SKIPPED, and so is a record whose start is not this locus. THE FIRST CONCRETE ALTERNATE IS THE ONE USED, so a record whose first alternate is the spanning deletion uses the second. THE SNP MASK WRITES N and --snp-mask-priority decides whether it beats a called SNP at the same site. --use-iupac-sample REPLACES A HET WITH ITS AMBIGUITY CODE taken from that sample's genotype rather than from the alternate allele. AND THE ARGUMENT CHECKS FIRE BEFORE THE TRAVERSAL: a priority flag with no mask is a CommandLineException and a sample the VCF does not have is a UserException.BadInput.

cases.why: 14 rows, no files that travel: one reference, one six-record VCF and a two-record mask, all written and indexed by the harness, run eight ways. Six produce a FASTA -- plain, masked, masked with priority, two IUPAC samples and a window that starts inside a deletion -- and two are argument refusals. One of the six is itself a refusal: a sample homozygous for a spanning deletion makes the tool write a space and the writer refuse it. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32283687055, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: The table CalculateContamination reads
suites.why: The tool that produces what CalculateContamination consumes, so this closes that chain from both ends. THE DEFAULT FILTER SET IS ELEVEN FILTERS rather than the walker's usual two, one of them parameterised at a mapping quality of 50. A SITE IS SUMMARISED ONLY IF ITS FIRST VARIANT IS BIALLELIC AND A SNP, so a triallelic site and an indel are skipped and only the first variant at a locus is looked at. THE ALLELE FREQUENCY BOUNDS ARE STRICT AT BOTH ENDS, so a site at exactly 0.01 or exactly 0.2 is excluded under the defaults. A VARIANT WITH NO AF IS SKIPPED, and if no variant had one the tool throws at the END of the traversal. A HEADER WITHOUT AF IS REFUSED BEFORE ANY READ IS TOUCHED, which is a different exception at a different moment. THE COUNTS COME FROM getBaseCounts, which counts A, C, G and T only, so otherAlts is over those four bases and not over the pileup's depth. AND THE TABLE CARRIES THE SAMPLE AS METADATA, taken from the first sample the read header names.

cases.why: 9 rows, no files that travel: two BAMs and three VCFs the harness writes and indexes, run eight ways. Six produce a table -- the defaults, opened bounds, a single site, a window with reads and no variants, and two over a second fixture that stacks six reads on one site -- and two are refusals, one before any read is touched and one at the end of the traversal. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32286128479, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: A samtools-style pileup and its optional columns
suites.why: THE DEFAULT FILTERS ARE THE WALKER'S PLUS THREE: this tool adds NotDuplicate, PassesVendorQualityCheck and NotSecondaryAlignment, so a duplicate that reaches CountReads never reaches this one. THE PILEUP IS FILTERED OF DELETIONS BEFORE ANYTHING IS PRINTED, so a deletion contributes to neither the base string nor the insert lengths, and the verbose column then reports a deletion count of zero at every locus because it counts them in the already-filtered pileup. WITHOUT A REFERENCE THE BASE IS 'N', which changes every base in the string that would have matched. THE FEATURES COLUMN IS ALWAYS PRINTED even when empty, so a line with no metadata ends in a trailing space. THE INSERT LENGTHS ARE ONE PER READ in pileup order, and a read with no mate has a fragment length of zero. AND THE VERBOSE COLUMN IS name@offset@length@mappingQuality per read, joined by commas, after the deletion count.

cases.why: 9 rows, no files that travel: one BAM and one metadata VCF the harness writes and indexes, run nine ways. Plain, verbose, insert lengths, both, metadata, no reference at all, the deletion read, the duplicate read (which produces an empty file) and the soft-masked stretch. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32288591691, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: Reference and alternate counts at heterozygous sites
suites.why: THE COUNTING CASCADE IS ORDERED: improper pair, then low mapping quality, then low base quality, then other-base, each of which continues, so a low-quality base on an improperly paired read counts as an improper pair and nothing else and rawDepth is the only counter that sees every read. OVERLAPPING MATES ARE ONE READ BY DEFAULT: COUNT_FRAGMENTS_REQUIRE_SAME_BASE keeps one element per read name and discards the pair entirely when the two disagree, COUNT_FRAGMENTS keeps the better-quality one either way, and COUNT_READS keeps both. A DISCARDED PAIR STAYS DISCARDED, because the filter remembers the names it deleted. THE SITE FILTERS ARE THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS: a non-biallelic site is skipped, a site with no het genotype is skipped, and two records at one position is a UserException that stops the run. A SITE BELOW --min-depth-of-non-filtered-base PRODUCES NO LINE AT ALL. THE SEPARATOR IS THE ONLY DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TABLE AND RTABLE and CSV is a comma. AND THE HEADER IS PRINTED BEFORE THE TRAVERSAL, so a run with no rows still writes one line.

cases.why: 10 rows, no files that travel: one BAM of five reads (an overlapping pair that agrees at one site and disagrees at another, a read at mapping quality 30, a read with one low-quality base, and an improperly paired read) and two VCFs, run ten ways. The three overlap modes, the two quality thresholds, a depth threshold, the two other output formats, a window with no sites, and two records at one position. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32289966161, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: Reference and alternate counts per locus
suites.why: EVERY LOCUS IN THE INTERVAL IS A ROW, because emitEmptyLoci is true, so a position with no reads is a row of zeroes rather than a gap. THE ALTERNATE COUNT IS TOTAL MINUS REFERENCE rather than the count of the alternate base, which the reference's own comment says. THE ALTERNATE BASE IS THE MOST COMMON NON-REFERENCE ONE and is N when the alternate count is zero. THE TOTAL IS OVER ACGT ONLY, so an N is in neither count and a deletion is filtered before the counting. THE BASE QUALITY THRESHOLD IS THE COLLECTOR'S rather than a read filter's, defaulting to 20, so a base at 19 is dropped while its read is kept. A REFERENCE BASE THAT IS NOT ACGT SKIPS THE LOCUS ENTIRELY, so an N in the reference produces no row even though emitEmptyLoci is true. AND THE TABLE'S HEADER IS A WHOLE SAM HEADER followed by the column names, with the sample taken from the read group.

cases.why: 6 rows, no files that travel: one BAM of seven reads the harness writes -- two carrying the reference bases, one all A, one all C, one all N, one with a base at quality 19 and one at mapping quality 20 -- run six ways. The default, two base quality thresholds, the reference's N run, a window with no reads at all, and the window covered only by the low-mapping-quality read. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32291444404, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: The normal-artifact training data
suites.why: The training data for Mutect2's normal-artifact filter, which this port already has. THE ALLELE IS CHOSEN IN THE NORMAL AND COUNTED IN THE TUMOUR. THE COUNTS HAVE SIX SLOTS, NOT FOUR: indices 4 and 5 are before-an-insertion and before-a-deletion-start, and an index at or above 4 is what makes the record's type INDEL. A SITE WITH NO NORMAL ALTERNATE IS SKIPPED, and so is one whose normal alternate is more than a fifth of the normal pileup. THE DOWNSAMPLE IS RANDOM BUT SEEDED, sharing one generator across the run, so the sites that survive depend on how many draws came before and a port that drew at a different moment keeps a different set. THE KEEP PROBABILITY HAS A FLOOR OF 0.05 and comes from the tumour's binomial p-value. A TUMOUR ALTERNATE ABOVE HALF THE TUMOUR PILEUP IS SKIPPED, and that test happens AFTER the draw, so it consumes a number either way. AND THE TABLE IS SIX COLUMNS with the downsample probability written as a double.

cases.why: 7 rows, no files that travel: two BAMs the harness writes, each carrying ten normal and ten tumour reads of forty bases, run seven ways with the shared random generator RESET before each so that every case means what the same command would mean on its own. The default window, a raised error probability, the whole forty bases, a single locus, a locus the normal has no alternate at, a normal sample the BAM does not have, and a second fixture whose tumour carries no alternate so the keep probability falls to its floor and the seeded generator keeps three loci of thirty. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32293455104, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: Copy-ratio segments called
suites.why: Pure arithmetic over a table: no reads, no reference, no walker. THE NEUTRAL BOUNDS ARE INCLUSIVE AT BOTH ENDS and are compared against 2^log2 rather than the log2 value. THE STATISTICS ARE COMPUTED TWICE, the outlier filter using the unfiltered mean and standard deviation and the calling threshold using the filtered ones. THE OUTLIER FILTER IS INCLUSIVE TOO. THE STANDARD DEVIATION'S DENOMINATOR IS ((n-1)/n) * totalLength, which is neither the population nor the sample form and is zero for a single copy-neutral segment. A RUN WHOSE COPY-NEUTRAL SET IS EMPTY CALLS EVERYTHING NEUTRAL, because the mean is NaN and every comparison against it is false. THE LENGTH IS THE INTERVAL'S, end minus start plus one. AND THE TOOL WRITES TWO FILES, the called segments and a legacy .igv.seg beside them whose columns are IGV's rather than GATK's.

cases.why: 16 rows, no files that travel: eight tables the harness writes, run through the tool and printed with the legacy .igv.seg beside each. A spread with two segments at exactly the bounds, an all-neutral set, a single copy-neutral segment (whose standard deviation divides by zero), an empty copy-neutral set, segments of very different lengths, moved bounds, a calling threshold of zero and inverted bounds. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32299022405, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: GC content and BED-weighted annotations per interval
suites.why: GC CONTENT IS OVER ACGT ALONE and the denominator is gc plus at rather than the interval's length, so an interval holding IUPAC codes (which the reader has already turned into N) has a smaller denominator than its length and one holding nothing else is a NaN. THE BED TRACK IS ZERO-BASED AND THE INTERVAL IS ONE-BASED, bridged by passing feature.getEnd() - 1 into an overlap computed against one-based coordinates. A MISSING OR NaN SCORE IS ONE rather than zero or a skip. THE ANNOTATION IS A LENGTH-WEIGHTED AVERAGE over the interval's length. AN OVERLAPPING TRACK IS REFUSED, the tool merging with OVERLAPPING_ONLY and comparing counts, so features that touch are fine and features that overlap are a UserException.BadInput. AND THE OUTPUT'S COLUMNS FOLLOW THE ANNOTATORS THAT RAN, in the order they were added.

cases.why: 7 rows, no files that travel: one FASTA and three BED tracks the harness writes and indexes, run eight ways. GC content alone over three windows, a window inside the reference's N run, two single bases, a mappability track, both tracks at once, an overlapping track, a touching one, and a run without the merging rule the tool requires. The @SQ lines carry a UR pointing at the container's own working directory, which is /work in the harness and in CI alike. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32300192529, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: Read counts per interval
suites.why: A READ IS COUNTED BY ITS START AND BY NOTHING ELSE: the overlap is computed against a one-base interval at the read's start, so a read spanning three intervals is counted in one and a read that starts before an interval and covers all of it is counted in neither. THE OVERLAP DETECTOR IS REBUILT PER CONTIG and holds only that contig's intervals. EVERY REQUESTED INTERVAL IS A ROW, in the order the interval argument produced, so an interval no read starts in is a row of zero. THE FILTERS ARE THE WALKER'S PLUS FOUR, one of them a mapping quality of 30. THE DEFAULT OUTPUT IS HDF5 AND THE TSV IS OPT-IN, carrying a SAM header, the sample as a read group and three columns. AND THE TOOL REQUIRES INTERVALS, refusing before it reads anything without them.

cases.why: 6 rows, no files that travel: one BAM of six reads the harness writes, run six ways. Four adjacent intervals, an interval a long read covers entirely without starting in, an interval on the contig with no reads, two intervals given out of order, the window covered only by the read below the mapping quality threshold, and a run with no intervals at all. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32305470003, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: Standardization without a panel of normals
suites.why: With no panel and no GC annotations the tool does the one thing its documentation calls standardization: fractional coverage, divide by the sample median, log2, subtract the median again. THE FIRST STEP DIVIDES BY THE SUM, so every later step is scale-free and doubling every count changes nothing. THE MEDIAN IS COMMONS-MATH'S, interpolating between the two middle values for an even count. THE LOG IS BASE TWO and taken after the division. THE MEDIAN IS SUBTRACTED AFTER THE LOG and is taken over the log values rather than over the originals, so it is not the logarithm of the first. A ZERO COUNT BECOMES NEGATIVE INFINITY. AND THE TWO OUTPUT FILES ARE IDENTICAL when there is no panel, the tool writing the standardized result as the denoised one as well.

cases.why: 13 rows, no files that travel: seven read-count tables the harness writes, run with no panel and no GC annotations. Six produce two files each, printed as the standardized and the denoised copy ratios -- five intervals, the same five doubled, an even number of intervals, a zero count, every count equal, and a single interval -- and the seventh, every count zero, is a refusal: the sum is zero, every fractional value is a NaN, and isPositive refuses a NaN median. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32307005892, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: The intervals a copy-number panel may use
suites.why: THE FILTERS SHARE ONE MASK AND RUN IN ORDER, so an interval failed by the GC filter is not in the population the percentiles are computed over. THE ANNOTATION BOUNDS ARE INCLUSIVE. THE LOW-COUNT FILTER IS STRICTLY GREATER, failing an interval when the number of samples below the threshold exceeds percentage times numSamples over 100, so one sample of two is not enough at the default fifty per cent. THE PERCENTILE FILTER TAKES ITS PERCENTILES OVER THE SURVIVORS ONLY, per sample, with inclusive bounds. A PERCENTILE OF ZERO IS SHORT-CIRCUITED TO A THRESHOLD OF ZERO rather than evaluated. WITH NEITHER ANNOTATIONS NOR COUNTS THE TOOL REFUSES. AND THE OUTPUT IS A PICARD INTERVAL LIST rather than the TSV every other copy-number tool writes.

cases.why: 11 rows, no files that travel: one annotated-intervals table and two read-count tables the harness writes, run eleven ways. Annotations at the default bounds, bounds leaving two intervals, bounds leaving one (which is a refusal, because a contig's only interval is filtered out), counts from one sample and from two, a raised low-count threshold, opened percentile bounds, both inputs at once, neither input, no intervals, and a -L naming the whole contig rather than the table's own intervals. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32308429691, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: ReadWalker traversal
suites.why: Every read-based tool inherits this traversal, so which reads reach apply and in what order is the tool's output. The probe is a real ReadWalker run through the real command line rather than a reconstruction: it records, per apply call, the read and the ReferenceContext window it arrived with. Two decisions are invisible from any tool's own output: the filter sits between the two read transformers, so it judges a read the walker never sees; and getReadInterval is null for a mapped read whose coordinates are not a valid interval, which hands the walker a read with no reference under it.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner. Refreshed to add the five -L unmapped runs: setTraversalBounds makes a traversal bounded when it has intervals or when unmapped reads were asked for, and loadNextIterator runs the interval query first and the unmapped query second, so the unplaced reads are a tail rather than an interleaving and -L unmapped alone is a bounded traversal of nothing else. It caught a divergence the class reading would not have: run without -R, a walker still receives a ReferenceContext whose *window* is the read's interval, with only its bases empty. The first version of the port handed over the fully empty context and would have reported a null window for every read of every reference-less run.

suites.title: PrintReads output bytes
suites.why: The first whole tool, and the first suite whose claim is bytes rather than decisions: the output BAM travels in the golden in full, base64, index included. Two header behaviours are measured with it: the @PG record the tool appends (ID, VN, CL, PN, with the ID taking a numeric suffix when it collides) and the fact that getHeaderForSAMWriter mutates the reads header in place. The dump installs htsjdk's JDK DeflaterFactory explicitly and records it in the golden, because --use-jdk-deflater does not restore it: GATK, like Picard, only ever installs the Intel factory when the flag is false, and that setter is static, so one earlier Picard call in the same JVM leaves GKL compressing everything that follows while the flag claims otherwise. The dump writes to a fixed directory rather than a temporary one, because the command line is recorded inside the output BAM's own @PG record: a random /tmp path does not make one golden row unstable, it makes every output byte unstable, and canonicalization cannot reach inside base64.

suites.title: UnmarkDuplicates and RevertBaseQualityScores output bytes
suites.why: G2's calibration gate: the second and third whole tools, so the marginal cost of an archetype member can be measured rather than guessed once PrintReads has paid for the engine. One dump covers both, which is itself part of the answer. Three behaviours are the reason for the case list and none of them is the transform. Both tools override getDefaultReadFilters to ALLOW_ALL_READS where PrintReads takes GATKTool's default of WellformedReadFilter, so on the same file the three tools emit different sets of reads and it is the filter rather than the apply that decides it; the wellformed case asks for the filter explicitly so the difference is visible in the golden. RevertBaseQualityScores aborts the whole run on a read with no OQ rather than skipping it or passing it through, so the output is whatever had been flushed and a port that passed the read through would produce a larger and healthier-looking file than the reference. And an empty OQ is the same as an absent one, because getOriginalBaseQualities returns null for both even though fastqToPhred of an empty string is happy and returns an empty array; that conflation is the reference's and is measured rather than inferred. The output BAMs travel in full, base64, indexes included, and the deflater is pinned and named in the golden because the factory is static and whoever touches it first wins for the life of the JVM.

suites.title: FixMisencodedBaseQualityReads, the fourth record-transform tool
suites.why: The fourth whole tool of the largest archetype, and the first whose transform can REFUSE THE FILE IT WAS GIVEN. Its apply is one line; everything worth measuring is elsewhere. IT DOES NOT OVERRIDE ITS READ FILTERS, so it takes GATKTool's default of WellformedReadFilter where UnmarkDuplicates and RevertBaseQualityScores replace the whole list with ALLOW_ALL_READS: three tools in one archetype and two different default traversals, which is why naming AllowAllReadsReadFilter changes what this one emits and would not change what the other two emit. A QUALITY BELOW 31 ABORTS THE WHOLE RUN with a message saying the read 'was correctly encoded', so a port that clamped would write a healthy-looking file the reference never wrote. THE REFUSAL IS A PROPERTY OF THE TRAVERSAL RATHER THAN OF THE FILE: the same fixture succeeds when an interval excludes the read that carries the low quality, which the corpus carries as two cases over one file. THE CHECK IS PER BASE AND AFTER THE SUBTRACTION, so the bases before the offending one are already rewritten when it throws. AND A READ WITH NO QUALITIES AT ALL PASSES THROUGH, because the loop never runs: '*' in a SAM is not a quality of zero.

suites.title: AddOriginalAlignmentTags, which aborts on an unpaired read
suites.why: The fifth whole tool of the record-transform archetype and the first that writes tags rather than changing the read. IT ABORTS ON AN UNPAIRED READ: addMateContigTag calls mateIsUnmapped, which htsjdk defines only for a PAIRED read, so an unpaired one throws IllegalStateException and the whole run stops. Three of the four measured runs abort on a fixture holding one unpaired read among six, and the one that succeeds does so because its interval excludes it. An unpaired read is ordinary in an ordinary file, so this is the tool's behaviour on ordinary input rather than an edge case. THE OA FORMAT'S COMMA ESCAPING CANNOT FIRE: it replaces a comma in the contig name with an underscore, and a comma is not a legal sequence name character at all, which the golden carries as htsjdk's refusal and the regex it quotes. A READ WITH NO NM STILL GETS AN OA and the missing field prints as the four characters 'null', because getAttributeAsString returns null into a format string. AN UNMAPPED MATE GIVES XM=* and an unmapped read the constant '*,0,*,*,0,0;'. The tags are read back off the output rather than inferred, and the reads that survive an aborted run are in the golden too: the writer had already flushed five of six.

suites.title: PrintDistantMates, which moves a read to its mate and sorts the result
suites.why: The sixth whole tool of the record-transform archetype, and three things in it are new to the archetype. IT EXTENDS THE DEFAULT READ FILTERS rather than taking or replacing them: getDefaultReadFilters starts from super's WellformedReadFilter and adds PAIRED, PRIMARY_LINE, NOT_DUPLICATE and MATE_DISTANT, a third pattern beside PrintReads which takes the default and UnmarkDuplicates which replaces it. Both lists are dumped rather than described. IT WRITES THE OA TAG WITH A DIFFERENT CONVENTION FROM AddOriginalAlignmentTags: both build 'contig,start,strand,cigar,mapq,NM;' and a missing NM prints as EMPTY here where the other tool prints the four characters 'null'. Both tools run over the same fixture so the two spellings of one missing field land in the same golden. IT OPENS ITS WRITER WITH preSorted = false where every other tool of the archetype passes true, and the transform moves each read into its mate's position, so traversal order and output order disagree by construction: the fixture's three surviving reads leave the traversal for chr2:600, chr1:2500 and chr2:150. undoDistantMateAlterations is measured as a round trip against the original record's own SAM text, tag block included, and on four OA values it cannot use.

suites.title: SplitReads, whose outputs come from the header rather than the reads
suites.why: The seventh whole tool of the record-transform archetype, and the first whose -O is a DIRECTORY and whose run opens more than one writer. THE SET OF OUTPUT FILES COMES FROM THE HEADER: createWriters takes the cross product of each splitter's getSplitsBy(header), so a read group no read belongs to still gets a valid empty BAM. THE CROSS PRODUCT DOES NOT DEDUPLICATE: two read groups with the same sample give the same key twice, prepareSAMFileWriter runs twice on one path, and the first writer is never closed because closeTool only closes what the map still holds. A NULL VALUE IS SPELLED TWO WAYS: a read group with no LB gives the key '.null' from the header, because addKey concatenates the Object, and '.unknown' from a read, because getKey substitutes UNKNOWN_OUT_PREFIX, so the file the header promises is not the file the reads go to and both exist. A READ WITH NO READ GROUP cannot answer any splitter, and whether that aborts the run is decided by a filter rather than by the tool: WellformedReadFilter's HAS_READ_GROUP drops it first, so both runs are measured, one with the default filters and one with that filter disabled. WITH NO --split-* the key is the empty string and one file is written, named after the input. AND EVERY FILE OF A RUN HAS A DIFFERENT HEADER: getHeaderForSAMWriter ADDS a @PG record to the reads header in place and returns the same object, and a writer serialises the header when it is created, so the nth writer's file carries n records for this one tool, with ids suffixed .1, .2 and so on. The on-demand unknown writer, created during the traversal, carries the most.

suites.title: AlignmentUtils.leftAlignIndels, and the shift that can go right
suites.why: The call LeftAlignIndels is built around, measured on its own because its interface is exactly measurable and needs no file: a cigar, a reference, a read and a start in; a cigar and two counts of removed deletion bases out. THE CIGAR IS WALKED RIGHT TO LEFT, accumulating an indel's ranges and resolving them only at an alignment block or the start of the cigar, so two indels with too few matching bases between them COLLIDE AND MERGE, which is a behaviour of the loop rather than of a named rule. normalizeAlleles CAN SHIFT RIGHT: it trims shared bases off the end and then off the front, and the front trim does startShift--, so the returned start shift is NEGATIVE on non-parsimonious input and leftAlignIndels reads that as newMatchOnLeftDueToTrimming. A port that typed the shift as unsigned would be wrong in a way no simple case shows, so the inner function is dumped on its own inputs with the ranges before and after, because it adjusts them as a side effect. A DELETION THAT REACHES THE START OF THE CIGAR IS DROPPED rather than emitted and the reference bases it removed are reported instead, which is what makes the tool move the read. TWO VALIDATIONS REFUSE RATHER THAN CLAMP, both IllegalArgumentException out of a util rather than a UserException out of a tool.

cases.why: A table of cigars over designed repeat structures and a table of allele ranges: homopolymers, a dinucleotide repeat, indels that cannot move, soft and hard clips the shift may not cross, two indels that collide, a deletion that walks off the start, both refusals, and the non-parsimonious ranges that shift right. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31516507658, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: LeftAlignIndels, the first tool of the archetype that needs the reference
suites.why: The eighth whole tool of the record-transform archetype and the FIRST WHOSE requiresReference() IS TRUE. THE REFERENCE A READ WALKER SEES IS THE READ'S OWN SPAN, no padding, so left-alignment is bounded by the read's own window rather than by the contig; the window handed to each read is dumped beside the read so a port cannot quietly widen it. A LEFT-ALIGNED DELETION CAN MOVE THE READ: CigarBuilder drops a deletion that ends up leading and reports the reference bases it removed, and the tool moves the read right by that many, which makes this the second tool of the archetype that changes a read's position after PrintDistantMates and for an unrelated reason. TWO CLASSES OF READ ARE PASSED THROUGH UNTOUCHED before the call rather than by it, an unmapped read and a read whose cigar has one element or none, and the fixture carries both. A RUN WITH NO -R IS REFUSED by Barclay rather than by the engine's requiresReference, so the message is an argument-parsing one. AND A PICARD CALL IN THE SAME JVM REPLACES THE DEFLATER FACTORY: this dump needs a .dict, so it calls CreateSequenceDictionary, which installs IntelDeflaterFactory into the static BlockCompressedOutputStream default and makes every BAM written afterwards carry GKL bytes whatever --use-jdk-deflater says. The dump records what the call left behind and pins the factory again before any run; #160 has the audit of the other dumps that do not. The call itself is measured by the left-align-indels suite.

suites.title: ClipReads, whose three clippers read the read in machine-cycle order
suites.why: The ninth whole tool of the record-transform archetype and the FIRST THAT WRITES A SECOND OUTPUT THAT IS NOT A BAM. THE QUALITY CLIPPER READS THE READ IN MACHINE-CYCLE ORDER, NOT IN REFERENCE ORDER: it walks i from the last base to the first but indexes with `isReverseStrand() ? readLen - i - 1 : i`, so a reverse-strand read is scanned from its front and the clip it emits is 0..clipPoint rather than clipPoint..readLen-1. The fixture's two quality reads carry the bad qualities at opposite ends of the array, so a port that walked the array backwards on both would find no clip point at all on the reverse one. THE REPRESENTATION DECIDES WHETHER THE WRITER SORTS: presorted is true only for WRITE_NS, WRITE_NS_Q0S and WRITE_Q0S, and the other three get a sorting writer, which the fixture makes observable twice over, by a soft clip that moves a read forward and by a revert that moves another backwards past it. HARDCLIP_BASES AND REVERT_SOFTCLIPPED_BASES REVERT BEFORE THEY CLIP, in apply, before the ReadClipper is constructed, so every clipper sees a read whose cigar and start have already changed. THE SEQUENCE CLIPPER IS A java.util.regex MATCH, case-insensitive, reverse-complemented for a reverse-strand read, looping until find() fails so one sequence can clip a read twice; its counts are keyed by the argument string in a TreeMap, which prints an upper-case argument before a lower-case one. THE CYCLE CLIPPER IS 1-BASED AND INCLUSIVE, clamps a stop past the end of the read and drops a range whose start is past it. THE ADAPTER CLIPPER DOES NOT FLIP FOR STRAND, and is the one place the tool adds a tag rather than removing bases. AND --read DROPS EVERY READ IT DOES NOT NAME rather than passing it through, so a --read that names nothing produces an empty BAM and a statistics file whose percentages are NaN, which is what String.format("%.2f", 0.0/0) prints in Java.

suites.title: TransferReadTags, the first tool of the archetype that is not a walker
suites.why: The tenth whole tool of the record-transform archetype and the FIRST THAT IS NOT A WALKER: it extends GATKTool and overrides traverse() itself, so there is no filter chain, no read transformer and no interval bound, and a port that reached for the read walker would apply WellformedReadFilter and drop reads this tool writes. The fixture carries a read with no read group for exactly that reason. It is also the first with TWO read inputs, walked in lockstep by query name with ReadQueryNameComparator, which duplicates SAMRecordQueryNameComparator. EVERY TAG IS TRANSFERRED AS A STRING, whatever it was: getAttributeAsString then setAttribute(name, String), so XI:i:42 arrives as XI:Z:42 and XN:f:1.5 as XN:Z:1.5, and the type is lost the same way every time. AN ALIGNED READ PAST THE END OF THE UNMAPPED FILE IS SILENTLY DROPPED, because the catch-up loop is `while (unmappedSamIterator.hasNext())` and when it runs out the loop simply ends: no exception, no warning, one fewer read in the output. THE WRITER IS NOT TOLD THE READS ARE SORTED, so htsjdk sorts a queryname header with SAMRecordQueryNameComparator and its six tie-breaks after the name; the fixture carries a name whose two records sit in the file in the order that comparator swaps. NO OUTPUT CARRIES AN INDEX whatever --create-output-bam-index says, because the output is queryname sorted. And the refusals come from four different layers: Barclay for a missing --read-tags, before the tool is built at all; Utils.validate for a coordinate-sorted -I, which is the only sort order checked and only on the aligned side; a UserException for an empty unmapped file beside a non-empty aligned one; IllegalStateException for an aligned read that is not in the unmapped file, from either of two throw sites with the same message; and IllegalArgumentException out of Utils.nonNull for a matched read missing the tag, naming the unmapped read rather than the aligned one.

suites.title: PrintReadsHeader, the smallest tool of the archetype
suites.why: The eleventh whole tool of the record-transform archetype, the second that is not a walker, and the SMALLEST TOOL IN THE ARCHETYPE: forty-six lines of which four do anything. It is measured for that reason as much as for itself, because G2's calibration gate asks what a member of this archetype costs at the margin and every measurement so far has been of a tool that does something. THE FINDING IS NOT ABOUT THIS TOOL: no BAM htsjdk wrote can carry a non-current @HD VN, because SAMFileWriterImpl.writeHeader(SAMFileHeader) calls the two-argument SAMTextHeaderCodec.encode, which is keepExistingVersionNumber = false, and BAMFileWriter overrides only writeHeader(String). The three-argument call that passes true is reachable only from the standalone block-copy reheader. The dump prints the header's own VN at the moment the writer is handed it: builtvn says 1.5 and the BAM that comes out says VN:1.6. htsjdk-rs's BamWriter keeps the header's version and its SamHeader::encode says in a comment that the writer passes true, so the port diverges on any input whose VN is not current; filed as htsjdk-rs#164. THIS TOOL REWRITES THE VERSION THROUGH THE SAME OVERLOAD, and writeHDLine(false) rebuilds the @HD line from a fresh SAMFileHeader, which also moves VN to the front; both are unobservable on any input htsjdk can produce and are recorded so a future hand-built fixture does not rediscover them. NO @PG IS APPENDED, because the tool reads getHeaderForReads() rather than getHeaderForSAMWriter(), which is the opposite of every writer tool in this archetype. THE OUTPUT IS TEXT THROUGH AN OutputStreamWriter WITH NO CHARSET, so it is the platform default; the output travels as base64 beside the charset's name so the two can be checked against each other. AND A HEADER WITH NO SEQUENCE DICTIONARY STILL PRINTS, while a run with no -I is refused by Barclay before the tool is built.

suites.title: PostProcessReadsForRSEM, and two null dereferences in its own guards
suites.why: The twelfth whole tool of the record-transform archetype, the third that is not a walker, and the first that groups the traversal into query-name runs of its own accord. A FOURTH getDefaultReadFilters PATTERN: it replaces the whole list with a single filter that is not Wellformed, Collections.singletonList(NOT_SUPPLEMENTARY_ALIGNMENT), so a supplementary alignment never reaches the tool and ReadPair's supplementaryAlignments list is dead code on this path. TWO OF ITS OWN GUARDS DEREFERENCE NULL. passesRSEMFilter opens with `if (read1 == null || read2 == null) { logger.warn(... + read1.getName()); }` and dereferences read1 inside the branch that exists because it may be null, so a query-name group holding only a second-of-pair kills the run: measured as `Cannot invoke GATKRead.getName() because "read1" is null`. And groupSecondaryReads collects into Collectors.groupingBy(isFirstOfPair), which produces no false key at all when every secondary is a first-of-pair, then calls read2Reads.size(): measured as `Cannot invoke List.size() because "read2Reads" is null`. The mirror image, every secondary a second-of-pair, names the OTHER list: `read1Reads.size() != read2Reads.size()` evaluates its left operand first, so which list is missing decides which name the JVM prints, and a port that assumed one message for both shapes would be inventing one. All three take the whole traversal down, so all three have their own fixture. THE OUTPUT ORDER IS PRIMARY PAIR THEN EACH SECONDARY PAIR, first-of-pair before second-of-pair, which is not the order the group arrived in, and a secondary finds its mate by contig plus getStart() == mate.getMateStart() and getMateStart() == mate.getStart() rather than by anything in the record that says so. THREE REASONS DROP BOTH READS: either read unmapped, different contigs, or a cigar that is not exactly one M, where `100=` is a single element and still refused because the test is on the operator. A PRIMARY PAIR THAT FAILS TAKES ITS SECONDARY ALIGNMENTS WITH IT, since the secondary loop sits inside the primary's if, while a secondary pair that fails on its own drops only itself. AND THE SORT ORDER IS CHECKED ON THE HEADER rather than on the reads, so a mis-labelled file is trusted.

suites.title: ConvertHeaderlessHadoopBamShardToBam, which copies rather than reads
suites.why: The thirteenth whole tool of the record-transform archetype and the FIRST THAT IS NOT A GATKTool AT ALL: it extends CommandLineProgram and implements doWork(), so there is no traversal, no read filter, no @PG record and no engine. THE SHARD IS COPIED BYTE FOR BYTE: FileUtils.copyFile between a header block and a terminator, so the output's data blocks are the shard's own bytes, not decompressed, not re-deflated and not re-blocked. Measured as a byte search rather than as a read round trip, because a port that read the records and wrote them back would produce a valid BAM with different bytes and every read-level assertion would still pass; the golden carries the shard's length, the output's three-part layout and whether the middle part equals the shard exactly. THE HEADER IS ENCODED WITH keepExistingVersionNumber = true, which is the other branch from the one PrintReadsHeader takes: this is the block-copy reheader path that htsjdk-rs#164 says is the only place the flag is legitimately true. THE HEADER BLOCK CARRIES NO TERMINATOR, because writeBAMHeaderToStream flushes rather than closes, so the empty gzip block appears exactly once and at the very end. AND A DONOR THAT IS NOT A BAM IS NOT REFUSED: reading a headerless shard as the header donor yields an empty SAMFileHeader under SILENT validation, and the tool writes a BAM whose header is nothing but @HD VN:1.6 with the shard appended. Nothing is added to a valid donor's header either, because there is no GATKTool to append a @PG. AND --use-jdk-deflater HAS TO BE PASSED HERE TOO: it is declared on CommandLineProgram rather than on GATKTool, so it reaches a tool with no engine, and CommandLineProgram installs IntelDeflaterFactory into the static BlockCompressedOutputStream default when it is absent, whatever the dump pinned beforehand. Measured: the header block is 177 bytes without the flag and 173 with it, and the JDK deflater produces 173 at every compression level, so the four bytes are the GKL deflater rather than a level. That is #160's mechanism seen from the other side, and the dump records the factory in force during each run rather than only the one it set.

cases.why: One donor BAM, one headerless shard built the way a Spark tool builds one, three runs, and for each the output in full. The shard is the donor's records re-encoded through BAMRecordCodec into a BGZF stream that is flushed rather than closed: slicing a finished BAM would not do, because htsjdk packs the header and small record data into one block and there is no boundary between them to cut at. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31540698514, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: GATKReport, the format both BQSR tools are written in
suites.why: The file format both BQSR tools are written in, measured before either tool that uses it: ApplyBQSR reads a recalibration table and BaseRecalibrator writes one, and both are this format, so the bytes are settled here or they are settled twice. THE COLUMN WIDTH IS THE WIDEST THING IN THE COLUMN, name included, and it is computed from the FORMATTED value rather than from the value, then frozen the first time getColumnFormat() is called. COLUMNS ARE SEPARATED BY EXACTLY TWO SPACES and the padding lives inside each column's own format, so a left-aligned last column carries trailing padding and a right-aligned one carries none; the dump prints every line with spaces replaced by underscores, because this format is decided by spaces and a diff cannot show them. ALIGNMENT IS RIGHT UNTIL A VALUE ASKS FOR LEFT: a value that is not numeric and is not one of null, NA, Infinity, -Infinity or NaN turns the whole column left-aligned, which is why the Flag column of booleans is LEFT and the Rate column holding NaN and -Infinity stays RIGHT. A COLUMN WITH AN EMPTY FORMAT IS Unknown AND A DOUBLE IN IT GETS %.8f rather than the column's %s, which is a special case in writeRow that nothing in the table declaration announces: measured as 0.50000000 and 0.33333333. A NON-FINITE DOUBLE ESCAPES ITS OWN FORMAT, because Double.isFinite decides and toString() is used instead, so a %.4f column holds -Infinity with no decimal point. A NULL IS THE FOUR CHARACTERS null whatever the column's type. AND THE TABLE HEADER CARRIES THE COLUMN FORMATS BUT NOT THEIR WIDTHS, so a reader recomputes every width from the values it parses; the dump round-trips each report through the parser and reports whether the second writing equals the first.

cases.why: Six reports: one column per data type with the two writeRow escapes in it, one that is numeric throughout so nothing asks for left alignment, one with two tables as a recalibration report has, and one per sorting over rows added out of order. Each travels as its whole text, as its lines with the spaces made visible, as the width and alignment the format computed for every column, and as whether a parse and a second writing reproduce it. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31570262261, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: RecalDatum, the counter every BQSR table cell is
suites.why: The counter every BQSR table cell is, settled before either tool that fills one: a recalibration table is an array of these, and every number BaseRecalibrator writes and ApplyBQSR reads comes from one. THE MISMATCH COUNT IS STORED MULTIPLIED BY 100000 and divided back on the way out, which is not the 10000.0 the comment beside the constant names, so the comment is stale and the constant is the behaviour; combine goes through both the divide and the multiply because it calls the other datum's public getter and hands the result to the incrementer. THE EMPIRICAL QUALITY IS AN int, not a double, since February 2025, so a %.2f of it prints two zeros after the point and never anything else. IT IS CACHED AND EVERY SETTER CLEARS IT: asked with a prior of 10 it answers 13, asked again with a prior of 45 it answers 13 again, and only after a setter that stored the observation count it already had does 45 give 44. THE SMOOTHING IS ONE ERROR AND TWO OBSERVATIONS APPLIED TWICE WITH DIFFERENT ARITHMETIC: the error rate adds them as doubles, the quality adds them to (long)(mismatches + 0.5), a truncating cast after a half that the reference itself marks TODO, so half a mismatch counts as one error and 0.49999 counts as none. A NON-INTEGER QUALITY DIFFERENCE TRUNCATES TOWARD ZERO because getLogPrior casts before taking the absolute value, so 29.5 against a prior of 30 gets the same entry as 30 does. THE PRIOR CACHE HAS 41 ENTRIES AND THE SEARCH HAS 61 BINS, so every difference past 40 shares -3200.2257913526446, and the cache is built from commons-math's FastMath.log rather than Math.log, which is why all 41 entries travel as raw bits. ZERO OBSERVATIONS SHORT-CIRCUIT to a log likelihood of exactly 0.0, an infinite or NaN one becomes -Double.MAX_VALUE rather than -Infinity, and quality zero with every base an error gives NEGATIVE zero. MORE THAN Integer.MAX_VALUE-1 OBSERVATIONS ARE RESCALED, errors included, by a Math.round of the scaled count. AND combine RECOMPUTES THE REPORTED QUALITY FROM BOTH SIDES' EXPECTED ERRORS rather than averaging: for two empty datums that is -10*log10(0/0) and therefore NaN, assigned to the field directly rather than through the setter that refuses NaN, and combining onto that NaN throws from QualityUtils.qualToErrorProb's qual >= 0.0 guard, which is the one reachable error the port cannot drop. The sign bit of that NaN is the processor's: x86-64 makes the floating-point indefinite and AArch64 the default NaN, so it is the single value the port compares as a NaN rather than as bits.
expect_contains: error	combine-onto-nan-reported	IllegalArgumentException	qual must be >= 0.0 but got NaN

cases.why: 332 rows: the seven constants including the two private ones, all 41 entries of the Gaussian prior cache as raw bits, twelve prior lookups chosen to cross the truncation and the clamp, thirteen binomial likelihoods covering both ends of the range and the rescaling above Integer.MAX_VALUE-1, seventy-two posterior maxima, sixteen datums read by every getter in the order that decides what the cache holds, nine cache steps, six combines, seven narrowing casts, fourteen refusals and the three event types. Every double travels as its raw bits as well as its decimal, because the port has to reproduce the bits and a decimal cannot show the last of them. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31571805427, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: The four BQSR covariates
suites.why: What a recalibration table is indexed by, settled before either tool that fills one. THE KEY MATRIX IS REUSED ACROSS READS OF THE SAME LENGTH AND IT DOES NOT LEAK: on a cache hit PerReadCovariateMatrix hands back the same int[][][] a previous read filled in and nothing clears it, so the dump runs the whole corpus twice, once with one shared cache as BQSR does and once with a fresh cache per read, and the two matrices agree in every cell, because every covariate writes a key at every position and ContextCovariate zeroes the array first on the one path that would leave a gap. A port may allocate per read and this is the measurement that says so. THE READ GROUP IS IDENTIFIED BY PU AND NOT BY ID, falling back to ID only when PU is absent: unit-rg1 and not rg1. A MISSING READ GROUP HAS THREE DIFFERENT ENDS: -1 from keyFromValue with an identifier the table does not hold, a NullPointerException for a read whose RG names a group the header does not declare, because getSAMReadGroupRecord answers null and getReadGroupIdentifier dereferences it, and IllegalStateException 'missing key 99' from formatKey. THE CONTEXT IS OF THE READ'S OWN BASES, reverse-complemented for a negative-strand read, with the low-quality tail overwritten with N first, and the first contextSize-1 positions get -1; an N poisons the following positions and the recovery after the first -1 walks BACKWARDS from the penalty position rather than restarting. THE CONTEXT KEY CARRIES ITS LENGTH IN THE LOW FOUR BITS, so A is 1, AA is 2 and AC is 66, and contextFromKey(4095) reads a length of fifteen out of a key holding thirteen bases and answers TTTTAAAAAAAAAAA, eleven characters of which come out of bits that were never written; both shifts take their distance modulo 32 the way Java's do, which is why the port uses the wrapping forms. THE CYCLE'S SIGN IS THE LOW BIT: cycle 3 is key 6 and cycle -3 is key 7, so key 1 decodes to negative zero, which is zero; second-of-pair flips the sign and a negative strand counts from the far end, and all four corners are in the corpus. INDEL CYCLE KEYS ARE -1 WITHIN FOUR BASES OF EITHER END, a cushion the substitution keys have none of. PAST THE MAXIMUM CYCLE IT IS A UserException whose message reports the ABSOLUTE value, so cycle -501 is refused with 'a larger cycle (501)'. AND A READ WITH BASES AND NO QUALITIES IS AN EXCEPTION rather than a covariate value, from the low-quality clip indexing an empty quality array by the read's length.

The corpus is the shared read-filter one plus ten reads that exist only to separate these covariates: a low-quality tail at each end, an N in the middle and an N in the first context, the same read on the negative strand, both second-of-pair corners, a nine-base read, a two-base read shorter than the indel context, an all-low-quality read the clip empties, and a read whose group is not in the header. suites.title: QualQuantizer and QuantizationInfo
suites.why: The map from every original quality score to the quantized one that replaces it: the last table a recalibration report carries, computed by BaseRecalibrator and read back by ApplyBQSR, so it is the interface between the two tools. EVERY LEAF INTERVAL IS CREATED WITH A FIXED QUAL, so getErrorRate returns qualToErrorProb of its own quality score and NOT the (nErrors+1)/(nObservations+1) the same method also implements; that second formula is only ever reached by a MERGED interval, and a reader of the method would assume the opposite. THE ERROR COUNT OF A LEAF SATURATES: it is (int) Math.floor(nObservations * errorProb) stored in a long, and Java's narrowing cast clamps rather than wrapping, so two bins of three billion observations at qualities 0 and 1 merge into an interval of 6000000000 observations and 4294967294 errors, twice Integer.MAX_VALUE and not the six billion the counts imply. THE MERGE SEARCH KEEPS THE FIRST MINIMUM, strictly less-than over an iteration in qStart order, so ties go to the leftmost pair, and ties are the rule on an empty histogram. THE PENALTY OF A MERGED INTERVAL IS A SUM OVER ITS LEAVES against the merged interval's own error rate, with every leaf at or below minInterestingQual contributing ZERO, which is what makes the low qualities free to merge; a global error rate of zero is a penalty of zero, tested before the leaves are walked. errorProbToQual ROUNDS AND THEN CLAMPS TO [1, 93] and WIDENS BEFORE IT NARROWS: Math.round returns a long that is assigned to a double before the cast to int, so the cast saturates and an error rate of zero comes back as 93; going straight from the long would wrap and answer 1. A QUANTIZED QUALITY OF ZERO IS STILL REACHABLE, because a leaf that was never merged returns its fixed qual directly and never goes through that function: a five-bin histogram at sixteen levels quantizes to 0,1,2,3,4. nLevels = 0 IS A NullPointerException, not an empty map, and an empty histogram is a NoSuchElementException with no message. AND QuantizationInfo COUNTS ITS LEVELS BY WALKING THE MAP FOR CHANGES, so 2,2,10,10,2,2,30 is four levels and not three, while noQuantization writes the identity over the first 93 entries only and leaves the 94th alone.
expect_contains: error	zero-levels	NullPointerException	Cannot read field "subIntervals" because "minMerge" is null

cases.why: 2414 rows: six histograms, each shaped for a different merge sequence, at seven level counts and three minimum interesting qualities, with the full quantization map of each and every interval of every final forest carrying its counts, its level, its fixed quality and both of its doubles as raw bits. Plus errorProbToQual at both ends of its range, QuantizationInfo's level count before and after noQuantization, the quantization report table of every histogram printed with its spaces shown as underscores, and seven refusals. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31573851625, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: NestedIntegerArray and RecalibrationTables
suites.why: The container a recalibration table is: four sparse arrays of RecalDatum indexed by covariate key, two of them special because the report writes them differently, and every shape taken from the covariates' own maximumKeyValue. Most of this is about which lookup answers null and which one throws, and the two are not where a reader would put them. THE VARARGS get() DOES NOT BOUNDS-CHECK ITS LAST KEY: it tests keys[i] >= dimensions[i] for the NESTED dimensions only and then indexes the leaf array directly, so an out-of-range last key is ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException where every other out-of-range key is null. AND THE SPECIALISED getNKeys() DO: get2Keys, get3Keys and get4Keys test every key including the last, so get(1,2,5) throws where get3Keys(1,2,5) answers null; they are documented as a performance specialisation of the same function and they are not the same function. EXCEPT get1Key, WHICH CHECKS NOTHING AT ALL, its comment saying the bounds check is done in the caller while no caller does it. A NEGATIVE KEY IS CHECKED BY NOTHING ANYWHERE, because every test is >= against the dimension, so it reaches the array index and throws in all five entry points. THE FIRST TWO DIMENSIONS ARE PRE-ALLOCATED and the rest are created on demand in put(). put() BOUNDS-CHECKS ONLY THE NESTED DIMENSIONS TOO, with two exact messages, 'Key 3 is too large for dimension 0 (max is 2)' and 'Exactly 3 keys should be passed to this NestedIntegerArray but 2 were provided', and its last key is an index error like get()'s. THE TABLE SHAPES COME FROM THE COVARIATES: read group 3x3, quality score 3x94x3, context 3x94x1012x3 and cycle 3x94x1002x3. combineTables STORES THE OTHER TABLE'S OBJECT ITSELF where the left table has no datum, so the two tables share it afterwards, measured as reference identity. AND safeCombine IS NOT SAFE: it allocates a new set of tables and combines BOTH arguments into it, so the first combine moves the left table's datums into the new table and the second combine mutates them, leaving the caller's left table holding the sum of both.

put	first-key-too-big	E:IllegalArgumentException:Key 3 is too large for dimension 0 (max is 2)
error	combine-different-shapes	IllegalArgumentException	Table1 2,3 not equal to 2,4

suites.title: Reading a GATKReport
suites.why: Reading a GATKReport, which is the direction ApplyBQSR uses: a recalibration report is parsed back into typed values, and which Java type each cell comes back as decides which branch RecalibrationReport's asLong, asDouble and decodeByte take. THE COLUMNS ARE CUT AT THE POSITIONS OF THE HEADER LINE'S WORDS: getWordStarts records every index whose previous character is whitespace and whose own is not, and splitFixedWidth cuts every data line at exactly those indexes, so no width is declared anywhere in the file and all of them are inferred from where the header's words begin. SO A HAND-EDITED FILE IS CUT IN THE WRONG PLACES: a value wider than its header swallows the next column's start and comes back as 'k  7', which a %d column then refuses with NumberFormatException, and a data line SHORTER than the header's last column start is a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, because substring is called with the header's indexes and no clamp. EVERY FIELD IS TRIMMED after the cut. A %d COLUMN PARSES TO Long AND NOT Integer, which is why asLong has an Integer branch it never takes from a parsed table while decodeByte has a Long branch it always takes. AN EMPTY FORMAT IS WRITTEN %s AND READ BACK AS A String, so the %.8f rendering an untyped double got on the way out comes back as the eight characters 0.50000000; null in a %s column comes back as the four characters and not as a null, while NaN in a %.4f column comes back as a Double. A PARSED TABLE IS DO_NOT_SORT whatever it was written with and its row ids are its indexes, which is what makes a parse and a second writing reproduce the first: four of the five parsed reports round-trip, and the one that does not was hand-written without the trailing colon the writer always emits after a table name. AND getReadGroups READS RecalTable0 AND RETURNS A SORTED SET, so zebra, alpha, alpha, middle comes back as alpha, middle, zebra.

error	read@ragged	NumberFormatException	For input string: "k  7"
error	empty-stream	UserException	input covariates table file for base quality score recalibration is empty.

suites.title: BQSRReadTransformer, the thing ApplyBQSR is
suites.why: A read in, the same read out with every base quality replaced. Everything measured before this (RecalDatum, the covariates, the tables, the quantizer, the report reader) is an input to this one function. THE ESTIMATE IS y3 + y4 - y2, not a sum of corrections: the read group's empirical quality is the prior for the reported quality's, and each special covariate then contributes its own empirical quality MINUS that posterior, while a NULL datum contributes nothing at all, which is not the same as contributing a zero delta. THE DATUM CACHE MAKES IT ORDER-DEPENDENT IN PRINCIPLE: getEmpiricalQuality(prior) computes on the first call and returns the cached value ever after, whatever prior is asked for, and the datums live in the table and are shared across every read, so the first read to reach a datum fixes its empirical quality for the whole run; measured directly, one datum asked with a prior of 25 and then of 45 answers 25.0 twice where a fresh datum asked with 45 answers 45.0, and the reference's own TODO says so. This corpus does not make it visible through apply, because each read reaches a different quality-score datum, and the dump runs the reads in both orders to show that. THE ROUNDING IS fastRound, (int)(x + 0.5) and not Math.round, so 0.49999999999999994 rounds twice and answers 1, and the result is then clamped to [1, 93]. A QUALITY BELOW preserveQLessThan IS LEFT ALONE ENTIRELY, not even quantized. --allow-missing-read-group COVERS A DIFFERENT CASE THAN ITS NAME SUGGESTS: it is tested against the COVARIATE's key, so it acts only when the recalibration report was written from a different set of read groups than the BAM has, and the read is then quantized but not recalibrated; a read whose group the covariate knows but whose TABLE holds no datum is a GATKException whatever the flag says, because the flag is tested before that lookup. constructStaticQuantizedMapping SORTS ITS ARGUMENT LIST IN PLACE, preserves every quality below MIN_USABLE_Q_SCORE as itself, and rounds in PROBABILITY space rather than in Phred space; its array is a Java byte[] of length 254, so the identity mapping it returns for an empty list wraps past 127 into negatives. AND WITH STATIC QUANTIZATION THE QUALITY IS QUANTIZED TWICE, first through the dynamic map and then through the static one, which the reference's own TODO calls out.
