Two more refusals happen while the definitions are built rather than while a command line is parsed: an ArgumentCollection field left null, and a field carrying both annotations. A duplicate alias is a third, and it is a construction failure rather than a shadowing rule, so an outer object and a nested one declaring the same name make the tool unusable before it sees an argument.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite. 42 rows, no corrections. The rows that carry the claim are the eight defs rows: the subclass's own field is index 0, its nested collection occupies 1 to 4, and the base class's two fields are 6 and 7.

suites.title: Barclay's --arguments_file
suites.why: G1.8's fourth slice, and the only argument that changes the command line rather than a field. When the special arguments-file argument is present, parseArguments reads the named files, splits every non-comment non-blank line on runs of whitespace, and calls itself again on the result. The file's arguments come first, because newArgs.addAll(Arrays.asList(args)) appends the original command line to the expansion rather than the other way round, and it does so wherever the arguments-file argument itself sat: a collection given a value in a file and another on the command line ends up with the file's first either way, and a scalar given in both is cannot be specified more than once rather than an override. The recursion is bounded by a set of file names rather than a depth, and every file named in a pass goes into that set including ones skipped for already being there, so a file that includes itself is read once and two files that include each other are read once each. The argument is not removed from the command line between passes: the recursion terminates because the second expansion is empty, not because the argument is gone. And the tag surrogates are reset between passes, because the first pass built keys the second would build again. Splitting is StringUtils.split, which collapses runs of whitespace, so an argument value containing a space cannot be written in one of these files at all.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite. 76 rows over 14 command lines, no corrections. The pair that carries the claim is file-then-command-line against command-line-then-file: the same three values in the same order both ways, because the expansion is what the original command line is appended to.

suites.title: Barclay's plugin descriptors
suites.why: G1.8's fifth slice, measured through GATK's own GATKReadFilterPluginDescriptor over GATK's own read filters rather than a stand-in, because --read-filter is this mechanism. A descriptor names a base class and a package, ClassFinder finds every implementation, and each one's arguments are registered as controlled by that descriptor, so every read filter's arguments are in the parser on every run whether or not anybody asked for that filter. What decides whether one is usable is validatePluginArgumentValues, which runs before the required check and rewrites the list it checks: a controlled argument that nobody set and whose filter nobody named is removed from the list rather than treated as optional, so a required argument of an unselected filter would not fire at all. The same argument set without its filter is an error that names the filter class rather than --read-filter, and builds the argument's own name from the short name, a slash and the long name with no guard, so one with no short name reports a leading slash. And the refusal of a name matching no filter is the descriptor's own validateAndResolvePlugins rather than the argument layer, which is why its wording is GATK's.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite. 48 rows over 11 command lines, no corrections. The rows that carry the claim are no-filter against dependent-without-filter: the same argument, left alone and set, with an unselected filter.

suites.title: NaturalLogUtils, and the rows that cannot depend on exp
suites.why: G1.9.1, and the layer AllelePseudoDepth stands on. Compared as raw bit patterns, because the question is whether a port built on a permissively-licensed exp lands on the same double and decimal rendering discards exactly that. The reference calls Math.exp; the port calls FDLIBM, measured at one ulp worst case against it by htsjdk-rs decision 0025, so this suite is not a bit-identity claim and does not pretend to be. It separates three things. First, the rows that reach neither exp nor log and are therefore exact by construction: logSumExp starts its accumulator at one rather than zero because the maximum's own term is skipped in the loop and folded in as that one, and the guard sum not equal to one then skips the log entirely, so a single non-infinite entry, a maximum with everything else at negative infinity, and a difference large enough that one plus exp of it rounds back to one all return the maximum untouched. Second, the rows that do call exp, which must land within one ulp, and the test reports the worst distance rather than only passing. Third, the refusal, which fires on the accumulator after the loop rather than on the inputs, so a NaN input reaches it and a negative infinity input does not, though the message names the inputs either way. A row diverging by more than one ulp means the port's arithmetic is wrong rather than that the exponential is approximate, which is the distinction the suite is built to make.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite. 42 rows, no corrections. It happens to be byte-identical to an Apple Silicon run, which says the two hosts' Math.exp agreed on these particular inputs and says nothing about the general case; the provenance is what makes it a golden.

suites.title: The Dirichlet fixed point, with its iteration count
suites.why: G1.9.2. The variational fixed point AllelePseudoDepth ends in, and where G1.9's open question lives. G1.9.1 established that a one-ulp exp is what enters here; this measures what the iteration does with it, and there are two ways that could go wrong which look identical unless they are separated. Amplification, where the difference grows across iterations. And a different iteration count, because convergence is a threshold test on distance1 over sum against a thousandth, so a difference far too small to see in the values can still put one side of that comparison on the other side of the threshold, after which the two runs do a different amount of work. The second would be far larger than the first, so the golden carries the count and the suite asserts it exactly, before comparing any value. The count is not exposed by the engine, so the harness replays the loop body with the same calls in the same order and checks its replay against the engine's own answer on every case, which the agree rows record. The weights rows are the control: effectiveLogMultinomialWeights is digamma arithmetic with no exp in it, so they carry no bound and must be bit-identical.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite. 29 rows, no corrections. The result it carries is the one G1.9 needed: every iteration count matches and the worst value divergence is zero, so the fixed point neither amplifies the exp difference nor crosses its convergence threshold differently.

suites.title: DecimalFormat, for the two patterns AllelePseudoDepth emits through
suites.why: G1.9.3. AllelePseudoDepth writes strings, not numbers, so java.text.DecimalFormat is part of its output. The Javadoc specifies HALF_EVEN and the pattern language and says nothing about the three facts that decide printed digits, each established here by measurement rather than by reading the class, which is GPL2 and may not be transcribed. First, it rounds the SHORTEST decimal form and not the value: formatting 0.1 to forty places gives 0.1 rather than the double's true 0.1000000000000000055511151231257827. Second, an apparent tie is settled by which side of the halfway point the double sits on, so 0.155 rounds down and 0.165 rounds up although the digit strings are the same shape, and only when the shortest form IS the value is it a real tie for HALF_EVEN to break on parity. Third, the two patterns disagree with each other at one place: where the rounding position falls before the first digit, #.## follows the value and #.#### rounds to even, so 0.005 and 5e-5 are the same shape one decade apart and go opposite ways. Values are bit patterns because a decimal literal in a golden would be re-parsed into a possibly different double, which for a suite about the last digit is the whole question.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite. 315 rows, no corrections, and byte-identical to the same container on Apple Silicon: nothing the formatter does here depends on the host. 630 strings compared and two values diverge, both above 2^53, where Java 17's pre-Schubfach digit generation stops producing the shortest decimal form. Below that line there is no divergence at all, measured on 903,121 values.

suites.title: String.format("%.Nf") over the shortest digits, not the exact expansion
suites.why: java.util.Formatter's %f conversion, which gatk_engine::java_format::format_decimals ports. IT IS NOT THE EXACT DECIMAL EXPANSION OF THE DOUBLE. The Formatter takes the digits Double.toString would produce -- the shortest that round-trip -- and pads or rounds THOSE to the requested scale. A VALUE WHOSE SHORTEST FORM ENDS IN 5 THEREFORE ROUNDS UP EVEN WHEN ITS EXACT EXPANSION DOES NOT: 2.675 is 2.67499999999999982... exactly, and Java prints 2.68 where a formatter working from the expansion prints 2.67, which is what C's printf prints. A LARGE VALUE IS PADDED WITH ZEROS, NOT EXPANDED: 1e300 is a one and three hundred zeros, not the 1000000000000000052504760255204420248704... the double actually is. THE ROUNDING IS HALF_UP ON THOSE DIGITS, not half-even, so 0.0625 at three places is 0.063 where Rust's own formatter answers 0.062. AND THE THREE NON-FINITE SPELLINGS HAVE NO SIGN ON NaN. Each value's Double.toString is printed beside its formattings, so the golden shows which digits the conversion started from.

cases.why: 54 rows, no files: twenty values, each with its Double.toString beside one to five formattings. The values are the four ties where the shortest digits and the exact expansion disagree, five magnitudes from 1e21 to Double.MIN_VALUE, the three percentages ClipReads prints, two carries that run the whole way up, zero and negative zero, a negative tie, and the three non-finite spellings. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32166667635, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: Double.toString over a corpus wide enough to say which values the port disagrees on
suites.why: Double.toString, over 1059 values. gatk_engine::tsv_table::java_double_to_string defers to Rust's shortest-round-trip formatter, and the pre-JDK19 FloatingDecimal does not always emit the shortest digits; the module note has said so since it was written, and the string-format golden caught one value. This establishes WHICH values differ rather than assuming there are none. The corpus is deterministic on both sides: twenty-seven named values, the powers of two across the whole exponent range, and a thousand bit patterns from splitmix64 seeded at one with the non-finite ones skipped. Nothing here is random. WHAT THE RUN ADDED: fifteen of the 1059 differ, which is 1.4 per cent, and in every one of them JAVA EMITS MORE DIGITS THAN THE SHORTEST. Three shapes. The smallest subnormal is 4.9E-324 upstream and 5.0E-324 here. 1e23 is 9.999999999999999E22 upstream, sixteen digits where two round-trip. And eleven values needing sixteen digits get a seventeenth: 7.2911220195563975E-304 against 7.291122019556398E-304. Every one of the fifteen parses back to the same double, so this is a rendering difference and not a value difference -- which is exactly why nothing had caught it until a golden printed the renderings themselves.

cases.why: 1059 rows, no files: twenty-seven named values covering both ends of the range, the neighbours of one, the boundaries of the exponent form and the four ties the string-format suite uses; thirty-two powers of two stepping through the whole exponent range; and a thousand bit patterns from splitmix64 seeded at one. Each row carries the double's bits as sixteen hex digits, so the comparison is on the value and not on a parse. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 32169248296, and byte for byte what this laptop produced.

suites.title: DD and DF, the annotation G1.9 was opened for
suites.why: G1.9.3, and the end of G1.9. AllelePseudoDepth emits its two keys as STRINGS through DecimalFormat at two and four decimals, which is what makes an oracle-backed suite possible at all for a chain that calls Math.exp: G1.9.1 measured the port within 1 ulp of the reference and G1.9.2 measured the fixed point at zero ulp, and the formatter is about twelve orders of magnitude coarser than a last bit. The suite therefore compares the formatted strings, which is the only thing the reference writes. Four behaviours are the reason for the case list, and none of them is the arithmetic. composePriorPseudoCounts memoises one array per allele count and hands out that array rather than a copy, so on the empty-evidence branch the posteriors ARE the memo and the closing subtraction zeroes it; every case is annotated twice with the same object, and the reference's own second answer for empty-evidence is NaN,NaN. The log10 branch's visitor receives (row, column) as (allele, read) and looks the mapping quality up at evidence().get(row), so a site with more alleles than reads throws IndexOutOfBoundsException and one with fewer floors each allele's row using an unrelated read's quality. The decay rate selects which intrinsics run: one Math.pow per read at the default, two when it is neither zero nor one, and none at zero, where the weights are null. And the guards put no key in the genotype at all, which is not the same as an empty one. The matrices are graded rather than symmetric, because a symmetric site gives every read the same weight and every setting of weightDecay the same answer.

cases.why: From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of the run that added this suite. 69 rows, no corrections, and byte-identical to the same container on Apple Silicon. All 46 calls match, including the two whose second answer differs from their first because the reference wrote through its own memo.

suites.title: CountBases, CountReads and FlagStat, whose output is a number rather than a BAM
suites.why: The first three tools whose output is a NUMBER rather than a BAM. All three are `ReadWalker`s whose `apply` is one line and whose whole answer is what `onTraversalSuccess` prints, so what they measure is the traversal and the formatting rather than any transform. THEIR DEFAULT FILTER IS THE ENGINE'S, WellformedReadFilter, so a malformed read is not counted by any of the three: a file holding nothing but two reads whose cigars disagree with their lengths counts 0, and 2 with the filter disabled. CountBases COUNTS read.getLength(), the number of BASES AND NOT THE SPAN, so twelve ten-base reads come to 120 whether they carry a deletion or an insertion. FlagStat's PERCENTAGES ARE COMPUTED IN float AND FORMATTED WITH DecimalFormat("#0.00"), which rounds HALF_EVEN where String.format("%.2f") rounds HALF_UP: two different roundings, and this is the one that reaches the output, 11 of 12 mapped coming out 91.67%. WITH NO READS AT ALL THE RATIO IS 0f/0f, so the percentage is NaN% , a real line of a real output and not an error. read2 IS TESTED BEFORE read1 AND THE TWO ARE `else if`, so a read carrying both 0x40 and 0x80 counts as read2 only. `singletons` AND `with_itself_and_mate_mapped` ARE BOTH INSIDE the paired branch, so an unpaired read contributes to neither however it is mapped. AND isUnmapped IS THE THREE-PART TEST rather than the 0x4 flag.

cases.why: 30 rows: three fixtures with their indexes, and eight runs of each. The corpus covers every branch of FlagStat's counter, an empty file where the percentages divide by zero, and a file holding only reads the default filter drops. Each fixture is run whole, over an interval that keeps half of it, and with WellformedReadFilter disabled. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31592539751, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: SATagBuilder, the SA tag a split read carries
suites.why: The first piece of SplitNCigarReads, whose `repairSupplementaryTags` marks every piece after the first as supplementary and calls `setReadsAsSupplemental`. A UNIT IS SIX FIELDS SPLIT WITH `split(",", -1)`, so `chr1,100,+,10M,60,;` parses with an empty NM where the zero-limit split would have dropped the field and refused it. THE THREE VALIDATIONS ARE POS, CIGAR AND MAPQ, each accepting `*`; NM IS NOT VALIDATED AT ALL, so `not-a-number` round trips. THE STRAND IS NORMALISED ON THE WAY OUT, the one field that does not survive a round trip. A UNIT BUILT FROM AN UNMAPPED READ IS `*,0,+,*,0,*;`, where the position and the mapping quality are the read's own zeroes and not `toString`'s defaults, which no read can reach. addTag PUTS A NON-SUPPLEMENTARY READ AT THE FRONT, and setReadsAsSupplemental MARKS EVERY READ BUT THE FIRST BEFORE BUILDING ANY TAG, so the primary is the first unit of every tag. EXISTING SA TAGS ARE PRESERVED AND STAY FIRST. THE PRIMARY IS NEVER UN-MARKED, so a family whose primary arrives with 0x800 comes out with no primary line at all. AND A FAMILY OF ONE WRITES NOTHING, because `setSATag` on an empty builder leaves the read alone rather than giving it an empty tag.

cases.why: 30 rows: nine tags that round trip, six that are refused, five units built from reads, and six families of reads set as supplemental to each other. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31597074001, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: OverhangFixingManager, the overhang clipper SplitNCigarReads writes through
suites.why: The second piece of SplitNCigarReads, and the one that decides what the output reads look like. overhangingBasesMismatch REFUSES THREE KINDS OF SPAN BEFORE COUNTING ANYTHING: below 1, above --max-bases-in-overhang, and STRICTLY LONGER than half the read's non-clipped length, where the division is integer and the comparison is `>`, so on ten bases a span of five is tested and six is refused while on NINE bases five is already refused. IT HAS TWO WAYS TO SAY YES: the tolerance, and a span where at least (span+1)/2 bases mismatch, so one mismatch out of two is a mismatch although the tolerance is one. isLeftOverhang AND isRightOverhang MIX STRICT AND NON-STRICT COMPARISONS, so a read starting exactly at the splice start is neither and one starting a base later is a left overhang. addSplicePosition RETURNS null BOTH FOR A SPLICE ALREADY HELD AND FOR A MANAGER WITH FIXING TURNED OFF, told apart only by what is held afterwards, and A SPLICE ON A NEW CONTIG CLEARS EVERYTHING SEEN SO FAR. THE QUEUE FLUSHES HALFWAY UNDER PRESSURE and completely on a new contig. THE FAMILY IS REPAIRED ON THE WAY OUT, NM, MD and NH cleared and the SA tags written, and only when writing is active. A SECONDARY ALIGNMENT IS WRITTEN BUT NOT CLIPPED unless --process-secondary-alignments is given. activateWriting A SECOND TIME IS A GATKException. AND THE MATE KEY IS name@0-or-1@start, whose digit is !isFirstOfPair when stored and isFirstOfPair when looked up, carrying the read's OLD start, so a mate already pointing at the clipped read's new position misses.

cases.why: 57 rows: twelve span decisions, eight overhang verdicts, three mate keys, six splice lifecycle steps, one refusal, seven runs of reads through the manager with every read they wrote, and six mate repairs. The two protected predicates and the package-private key builder are reached by reflection. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31598493960, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: SplitNCigarReads, the RNA-seq splitter the last two suites were built for
suites.why: The thirteenth whole tool of the record-transform archetype, and the first that is a MultiplePassReadWalker: the input is traversed TWICE, the first pass recording which reads the overhang clipper moved and the second writing them out with their mates repaired. A READ WITH k N ELEMENTS BECOMES k+1 READS, each keeping every base and soft clipping the rest, so 3M2N5M comes out 3M5S and 3S5M. A SECTION BESIDE A DELETION IS TRIMMED BEFORE THE CLIP, and N-D-N is an IllegalArgumentException naming the cigar unless --refactor-cigar-string merges the motif into one N first; the refactor merges ONE motif per two elements skipped, so 3M2N1D2N1D2N2M comes out 3M5N1D2N2M. A CIGAR ENDING IN N EMITS ONE PIECE AND LOSES THE N; A CIGAR BEGINNING WITH N IS PASSED THROUGH UNTOUCHED. THE MAPPING QUALITY TRANSFORM REWRITES 255 AND ONLY 255, to 60, unless skipped. ITS DEFAULT FILTER IS ALLOW_ALL_READS, so a malformed read is still written. AN MC TAG IS REWRITTEN to what the mate's cigar will become, computed by splitting an artificial read carrying it. A SECONDARY ALIGNMENT IS NOT SPLIT unless --process-secondary-alignments is given. THE OUTPUT HEADER CARRIES TWO @PG RECORDS, `GATK SplitNCigarReads` and `GATK SplitNCigarReads.1`, because onTraversalStart asks for the header once and createSAMWriter asks again. AND ITS WRITER SORTS: createSAMWriter(OUTPUT, false), so a family's second piece lands at its own coordinate rather than beside its first.
expect_contains: error	ndn	java.lang.IllegalArgumentException:Cannot split this read (might be an empty section between Ns, for example 1N1D1N): 3M2N1D2N5M

cases.why: 114 rows: seven cigars through the NDN refactor, five input BAMs with their indexes, and ten runs of which nine finish, each with its header, its command line, its output BAM, its index and every record it wrote. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31599678016, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: MethylationTypeCaller, the first tool of the archetype whose output is a VCF
suites.why: The last non-Spark record-transform tool GATK wrote itself, and the first whose output is a VCF. THE STRAND IS CHOSEN BY THE REFERENCE BASE AND NOT BY THE READS: a C is counted from forward reads alone and a G from reverse ones alone, so a C covered only by reverse reads produces no record at all. DP IS THE WHOLE PILEUP while the two counts are one strand and two bases, so the numbers of a record do not add up: DP=5 where the counts are 1 and 1. A SITE WITH NO METHYLATED COVERAGE WRITES NOTHING, `unconverted + converted > 0`. THE FORWARD CONTEXT IS getBases(0, 2) AND THE REVERSE CONTEXT IS getBases(2, 0) REVERSE COMPLEMENTED, so both read from the C of their own strand, and a site near the contig edge gets a SHORTER context rather than an error: CC at 59 and C at 60 of a sixty-base contig. AN UNMAPPED READ IS DROPPED BY THE LOCUS WALKER'S FILTERS and a deletion contributes no base. THE SAMPLES ARE THE READ GROUPS' SAMPLES SORTED THEN DEDUPLICATED and the records carry no genotypes, so every record of a two-sample header ends with two `./.` columns. AND THE DEFAULT HEADER CARRIES A ##GATKCommandLine LINE WITH THE RUN'S OWN DATE, which no golden can hold: three runs pass --add-output-vcf-command-line false and the fourth is dumped with its date masked.

cases.why: 74 rows: two input BAMs with their indexes, the reference bases, and four runs of which three are comparable line by line while the fourth contributes only its masked command-line header. From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31601435587, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: GetSampleName, the smallest tool of the reporting-walker archetype
suites.why: The second tool of the reporting-walker archetype and the smallest: `traverse` is empty and everything happens in onTraversalStart. IT WRITES EVERY DISTINCT SAMPLE ONE PER LINE WITH NO TRAILING NEWLINE, so `sample1` is seven bytes and two samples are eleven; the file's length is dumped beside its text because that is the only place the missing newline shows. distinct() KEEPS THE FIRST OCCURRENCE AND ITS ORDER, so two read groups naming one sample give one line and `zebra` then `alpha` come out unsorted. A HEADER WITH NO READ GROUPS TAKES THE SECOND REFUSAL AND NOT THE FIRST, because getReadGroups() returns an empty list rather than null, so the guard about "no header or no read groups" is unreachable from a BAM. A READ GROUP WITH NO SM WRITES THE FOUR LETTERS `null` and the tool finishes. --use-url-encoding HAS NO DEFAULT IN THE SOURCE AND IS STILL OPTIONAL. suites.title: SAMPileupCodec, the samtools mpileup format CheckPileup reads as its truth
suites.why: THE FIELD COUNT MUST BE 4 TO 6, WHICH IS NOT THE FORMAT'S. THE BASES COLUMN IS A LITTLE LANGUAGE: `.` and `,` are the reference base, `*` is a deletion, `$` ends a read and consumes NO quality, `^` eats the NEXT character as a mapping quality, and `+`/`-` skip an indel whose length is the number that follows. THE QUALITY STRING IS THEREFORE CONSUMED AT A DIFFERENT RATE FROM THE BASES STRING, which is why leftover qualities are their own error and leftover bases are unreachable. A DELETION BECOMES THE LETTER `D`, which is not a base the reads column itself would accept. A COVERAGE OF ZERO RETURNS EARLY, so a line whose bases and qualities are nonsense parses. TWO MESSAGES CARRY TYPOS a port has to carry too, "THe SAM pileup line" and "this codes is only valid". AN N FOLDS TO N and every other base comes out upper case. AND canDecode IS THE EXTENSION AND NOTHING ELSE, case-insensitively, with one block-compressed extension stripped first.

suites.title: The tsv table format, under every .table file GATK writes
suites.why: GATK's own table format and the first shared piece of CalculateContamination. METADATA IS A TAGGED COMMENT, `#<METADATA>key=value`: a hand-written `#sample=s1` looks like metadata and is a plain comment. AND THE MAP IS FILLED BY processCommentLine ITSELF, so a subclass that overrides that method without calling super LOSES EVERY PAIR; the same file read twice, once with an override and once without, gives an empty map and `sample=s1`. A VALUE IS QUOTED ONLY WHEN IT HAS TO BE: a space and a comma pass through bare, a tab, a quote and a backslash force quotes, and a value beginning with the comment prefix is written unquoted. THE ESCAPE IS THE BACKSLASH inside quotes. THE HEADER IS WRITTEN EVEN WITH NO RECORDS AND EVEN WHEN IT WAS NEVER ASKED FOR. A DOUBLE IS String.valueOf's SPELLING, so a third is 0.3333333333333333, 1e-7 is 1.0E-7 and the non-finite ones are NaN and Infinity. A ROW OF THE WRONG WIDTH IS THE SAME REFUSAL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, naming the file, the line and both counts. A COLUMN THE HEADER LACKS IS A PLAIN IllegalArgumentException AND NOT A UserException. suites.title: PersistenceOptimizer, the watershed under the kernel segmenter
suites.why: The watershed under the kernel segmenter, which is how CalculateContamination picks changepoint candidates: given one-dimensional data it returns every local minimum ordered by topological persistence. THE GLOBAL MINIMUM IS PREPENDED to the sorted run, so the first index is not part of it and the first persistence is the whole range rather than any pair's. THE INDICES ARE SORTED BY Comparator.comparingDouble, WHICH IS Double.compare, so -0.0 SORTS BELOW 0.0 and NaN SORTS ABOVE EVERYTHING: on [0.0, -0.0, 0.0, -0.0] the global minimum is index 1 and one persistence comes out as NEGATIVE ZERO, and on data holding a NaN the NaN is the global maximum and two persistences are NaN. A port comparing with `<` would order neither the same way. THE SORT IS STABLE, so a plateau is entered from the left and its LEFTMOST point is the local minimum. MERGING KEEPS THE COMPONENT WITH THE LOWER MINIMUM and, on a tie, the LOWER COLOUR, which is the earlier component and not the earlier index, while the local maximum takes the colour of the point on its left read AFTER the merge. A SINGLE POINT HAS NO PAIRS, so the answer is one index and a persistence of zero. AND EMPTY DATA IS REFUSED by the argument check, "Data must contain at least one element."
expect_contains: error	empty	java.lang.IllegalArgumentException:Data must contain at least one element.

suites.title: RemoveNearbyIndels, the first variant transform
suites.why: The first member of the variant-transform archetype: a VariantWalker that buffers one indel at a time and drops any PAIR of indels closer than a spacing, keeping whatever non-indels sat between them. THE DISTANCE IS END TO START, `right.getStart() - left.getEnd()`, so a deletion's length counts against it and the test is STRICT: two indels exactly the spacing apart are kept and one base closer are both dropped, which the golden holds at 5 and at 4 for the same file. AND lastIndel IS UPDATED EVEN WHEN THE INDEL WAS JUST THROWN AWAY, so a third indel is measured against one that never reached the output: three indels in a row lose all three, and at a spacing of 1000 an indel 790 bases past a discarded one is discarded too. THROWING OUT A PAIR EMITS THE NON-INDELS BETWEEN THEM. `nearby` REQUIRES THE SAME CONTIG, so a contig boundary flushes. THE LAST INDEL OF A FILE IS KEPT BY A REFERENCE COMPARISON, `vc == lastIndel`, and not by an equality: without it the buffered indel would be measured against ITSELF and dropped, since start minus end is below any positive spacing. AND `isIndel` IS `getType() == INDEL`, WHICH A MIXED SITE IS NOT: a record whose alternates are all a different length from the reference is an INDEL and buffers like one, while a record carrying a snp and an insertion side by side is MIXED, so it is never buffered and cannot pair with anything, and one carrying two snps is a plain SNP. AND THE HEADER IS REBUILT FROM THE INPUT'S SORTED METADATA plus the tool's own lines, so a ##GATKCommandLine carrying the run's date is added, which is masked in the golden.

suites.title: UpdateVCFSequenceDictionary, the second variant transform

suites.title: leftAlignAndTrim, the workhorse under LeftAlignAndTrimVariants
suites.why: The workhorse under LeftAlignAndTrimVariants, measured on its own before the tool. It slides an indel as far left as the reference lets it, WIDENING ITS OWN WINDOW as it goes: `leadingBases = min(maxLeadingBases, 10)` then doubling, so an insertion that walks 19 bases costs two passes. THE LOOP ONLY CONTINUES WHEN THE SHIFT REACHED THE EDGE of the slice, so A WINDOW THAT IS TOO NARROW SILENTLY EMITS A RECORD THAT IS NOT LEFT ALIGNED: the same deletion at max-leading-bases 2 lands at 15, at 10 lands at 49, at 20 at 39, and only a wide enough window reaches the run's start. A SHIFT OF ZERO RETURNS THE SAME OBJECT, and so do maxLeadingBases <= 0 and a non-indel, which is a TYPE test, so a MIXED site is never aligned. THE START AND THE END MOVE BY DIFFERENT AMOUNTS, start by shifts.left and stop by shifts.right, and with trimming on an untrimmed pair of alleles loses its shared trailing base while with trimming off the record moves at full length. GENOTYPES ARE REMAPPED THROUGH THE SAME MAP the alleles came out of, and an allele outside that map would become NO_CALL, which no valid record can reach: htsjdk refuses to build a VariantContext whose genotype calls an allele it does not list.

suites.title: trimAlleles, the other half of LeftAlignAndTrimVariants
suites.why: The other half of what LeftAlignAndTrimVariants does, and what the multiallelic splitter calls on every biallelic it makes: cut the bases every allele shares. ONE ALLELE OF LENGTH ONE STOPS EVERYTHING, `anyMatch(a -> a.length() == 1 && !a.equals(Allele.SPAN_DEL))` returning the input untouched, so a record carrying a snp beside a deletion is never trimmed however much its other alleles share. THE SPANNING DELETION IS THE ONE EXCEPTION to that test, and neither it nor a symbolic allele is fed to the comparison, though both are kept in the output, so `ACGT,AGT,*` still trims to `AC,A,*`. THE FORWARD TRIM IS A NEGATIVE SHIFT, `startTrim = -shifts.getLeft()`, normalizeAlleles being asked to move alleles that start at index 0 and can only go backwards. AN ALLELE TRIMMED TO NOTHING GETS ONE BASE BACK, at the END when nothing was trimmed from the front and at the START when something was, which is the only reason a record keeps an anchor base. THE INNER trimAlleles TAKES AN INCLUSIVE INDEX, so the caller passes startBasesToClip - 1 and -1 means trim nothing, and it returns the INPUT ITSELF when that index is -1 and the reverse trim is 0. THE START MOVES BY fwdTrimEnd + 1 AND THE END IS RECOMPUTED from the reference allele's new length rather than by subtracting the reverse trim. AND THE ALLELE MAP IS A LinkedHashMap here where leftAlignAndTrim uses a HashMap, so the output keeps the input's order.

suites.title: splitVariantContextToBiallelics, what --split-multiallelics does
suites.why: What --split-multiallelics does in LeftAlignAndTrimVariants: one record with N alternates becomes N records with one each. A NON-VARIANT RECORD BECOMES AN EMPTY LIST rather than a list of one, so it disappears; A BIALLELIC ONE IS RETURNED AS THE SAME OBJECT, untrimmed, so the trimming every split record gets is not applied to one that did not need splitting. ONE HET-NON-REF GENOTYPE ANYWHERE CHANGES THE RULE FOR EVERY RECORD: `hasHetNonRef` swaps the assignment method to SET_TO_NO_CALL_NO_ANNOTATIONS for all of them, so a single 1/2 call in one sample empties the calls of every sample in every output record and strips every attribute. THE ATTRIBUTE FILTER IS A NEGATED DISJUNCTION, so AC, AF and AN survive a normal split, AND THEY ARE THEN RECOMPUTED FROM THE GENOTYPES: three diploid samples give AN=6 and AF=0.16666666666666666, and A RECORD WITH NO GENOTYPES LOSES THEM ALTOGETHER, the recomputation having nothing to count. EVERY OUTPUT IS RIGHT TRIMMED and only left trimmed when asked, so two alternates of different lengths come out AT DIFFERENT POSITIONS, 102-103 and 103-103 from one record. AND THE GENOTYPES ARE SUBSET rather than remapped: with no likelihoods to go on, BEST_MATCH_TO_ORIGINAL turns an allele that is not in the pair into the REFERENCE, so A/G becomes A/A in the record that kept C.

suites.title: LeftAlignAndTrimVariants, the tool
suites.why: The tool the last three bricks were built for. Its own logic is short: choose a window, call leftAlignAndTrim, remember the record just written. THE WINDOW IS BOUNDED BY THE PREVIOUS RECORD, min(maxLeadingBases, distanceToLastVariant - 1), measured from that record's END to this one's START, AND THE PREVIOUS RECORD IS THE ONE AS WRITTEN, NOT AS READ: lastVariant is the ALIGNED record, which has moved left, so aligning a variant RELAXES the bound on the next. Two indels a base apart in the input are eight apart by the time the second is measured, and both move. A NEW CONTIG IS Integer.MAX_VALUE AWAY, so the bound does not cross one. AN INDEL LONGER THAN --max-indel-length IS WRITTEN UNCHANGED and STILL BECOMES lastVariant, so it bounds the record after it though it was never aligned: the same file gives a deletion at 30 by default and at 34 with --max-indel-length 5. --dont-trim-alleles passes !dontTrimAlleles down, so a record moves without shrinking. --split-multi-allelics SPLITS FIRST AND ALIGNS EACH PIECE, and the pieces bound EACH OTHER through the same lastVariant, so one record at 17 becomes two at 10 and 12 rather than two at 10. AND THE HEADER'S CONTIG LINES COME FROM THE REFERENCE, so a contig the input never mentions is in the output header, carrying assembly=reference.fasta.

suites.title: The genotype index combinatorics under every PL array
suites.why: The combinatorics under every PL array, and the piece between LeftAlignAndTrimVariants and a genotyped vcf: which genotype each index of a likelihood vector means, and where a genotype lands when the allele list changes. THE INDEX IS A SUM OF BINOMIALS, `indexOfFirstGenotypeWithAllele(ploidy - n, allele)` summed over the alleles from highest to lowest, and THE NUMBER OF GENOTYPES IS THAT SAME FUNCTION at the allele count, C(alleles + ploidy - 1, alleles - 1), so a triploid site with four alleles has twenty genotypes and not sixty-four. THE CANONICAL ORDER is what GenotypeAlleleCounts walks: 0/0, 0/1, 1/1, 0/2, 1/2, 2/2. A GENOTYPE IS A MULTISET, so the pairs of allele and count may come in ANY ORDER and give the same index, while a count of zero contributes nothing; AN ODD-LENGTH COUNT ARRAY IS THE ONLY REFUSAL. PLOIDY ZERO HAS EXACTLY ONE GENOTYPE, the empty one at index 0. AND subsettedPLIndices IS A PERMUTATION, NOT A FILTER: keeping the alleles in the order 0, 2, 1 of three gives 0,3,5,1,4,2, and keeping only the reference gives a single index.

suites.title: subsetAlleles, what a split does to a genotype's likelihoods
suites.why: What splitVariantContextToBiallelics does to a genotype carrying likelihoods, which the split port refuses for want of a measurement. THE NEW PLs ARE THE OLD ONES PERMUTED AND THEN RESCALED by subtracting the maximum, so the smallest phred of the subset is 0 whatever it was: 50,0,60,40,30,70 keeping the SECOND alternate becomes 10,0,30. THE GQ IS RECOMPUTED FROM THE NEW PLs EVEN WHEN NOTHING IS DROPPED, so keeping all three alleles leaves the PLs untouched and changes the GQ from 50 to 30, and it is KEPT ONLY when the subset is the reference alone. A PL ARRAY OF THE WRONG LENGTH IS DROPPED ENTIRELY, along with the GQ, without a word. A HOM-REF OR NO-CALL GENOTYPE WITH GQ 0 IS NO-CALLED before the method is consulted, and IF ITS DP IS ALSO 0 EVERYTHING IS CLEARED. USE_PLS_TO_ASSIGN no-calls only when the best genotype is the reference AND the log10 GQ is above SUM_GL_THRESH_NOCALL, which is a GQ near zero, so a CONFIDENT hom-ref is called hom-ref and an uninformative one is not. THE AD IS PERMUTED, NOT SUMMED. POSTERIORS AND PRIORS ARE REMOVED WHATEVER HAPPENS while any other attribute is kept. AND SET_TO_NO_CALL EMPTIES THE CALL AND KEEPS EVERYTHING ELSE where SET_TO_NO_CALL_NO_ANNOTATIONS keeps only the depth: two names one word apart, two different genotypes out.

From the pinned container on a real x86-64 runner, published as the golden-pending artefact of run 31721036590, and byte for byte what an Apple Silicon laptop produced.

suites.title: Splitting a record whose genotypes carry likelihoods
suites.why: The junction between the splitter and the subsetting: what a real genotyped vcf goes through, which split-biallelics measured without likelihoods and subset-alleles measured one genotype at a time. EVERY OUTPUT RECORD CARRIES ITS OWN SUBSET of the PLs, so one record with two alternates leaves two whose likelihood vectors are different permutations of the same six numbers, each rescaled on its own, with its own GQ. AND THE CALL DOES NOT FOLLOW THE PLs: under BEST_MATCH_TO_ORIGINAL a sample whose alternate this record dropped is called HOM-REF even where its own subset likelihoods make the heterozygote the most likely genotype by 10 phred, so `A/G` comes out `A/A` beside PLs of `10,0,30`. THE AC AND AF ARE RECOMPUTED FROM THE SUBSET CALLS, so a sample counts towards one record and not the other, and a hom-alt gives AF=1.0 in its own record and 0.0 in the other. ONE HET-NON-REF GENOTYPE STILL EMPTIES EVERYTHING, calls, likelihoods, AD and attributes, keeping only the depth. THE AD IS SPLIT BY ALLELE and the dropped alternate's depth is gone rather than folded into the reference. A SAMPLE WITHOUT LIKELIHOODS KEEPS ITS GQ beside one that has them and loses it. AND THE TRIMMING STILL HAPPENS AFTER ALL OF IT, so one record moves to 100-102 while its genotypes are being rewritten.

suites.title: VariantFiltration, the FILTER column
suites.why: A variant transform whose whole job is the FILTER column: JEXL expressions at the site and at the genotype, a clustered-SNP test that looks at neighbours, and a mask read from a second file. THE FILTER SET IS SEEDED FROM THE RECORD'S OWN FILTERS, so an existing filter survives a run that adds another, but THE ORDER IN THE FILE IS THE WRITER'S AND NOT THE TOOL'S: `OldFilter` plus `LowQD` comes out `LowQD;OldFilter`, and two expressions given as LowQD then LowDP come out `LowDP;LowQD`. AN EMPTY SET BECOMES `PASS` AND NOT NOTHING, which the source comments on, EXCEPT under --invalidate-previous-filters where the same emptiness leaves a `.` and wipes the filter the record arrived with. THE CLUSTER TEST IGNORES NON-SNPs as candidate and as neighbour, and a window below 1 disables it: three SNPs within 20 bases are all SnpCluster while the indel between them passes, and the same file at a window of 5 filters nothing. A GENOTYPE FILTER WRITES FT AND KEEPS THE CALL, unless --set-filtered-genotype-to-no-call which replaces it with `./.`, AND THE FT COLUMN IS PER RECORD: it appears only where at least one genotype was filtered, the unfiltered samples of that record then carrying `PASS`, while a record with nothing filtered has no FT field at all. AN EXISTING FT IS CARRIED beside the new names. --invert-filter-expression FLIPS THE MATCH, so the column carries the complement. AND A MISSING ANNOTATION IS NOT A FAILURE unless --missing-values-evaluate-as-failing, which is what decides a record that lacks the field entirely.

suites.title: GatherVcfsCloud, two gathering modes and four refusals
suites.why: Concatenating vcfs that are already in order, which sounds like `cat` and is not. THERE ARE TWO ORDER CHECKS AND THEY THROW DIFFERENT CLASSES: the validation before writing compares the FIRST record of each file and refuses with an IllegalArgumentException, while the conventional writer compares the LAST record written against the next file's first and refuses with an IllegalStateException naming both positions, so files overlapping in the middle pass one and are caught by the other. --disable-contig-ordering-check DOES NOT DISABLE THE CHECK BUT WEAKENS IT, comparing positions only within a contig, and the result is an INVALID FILE: a chr2 shard gathered before a chr1 shard is accepted and the output holds chr2:100 followed by chr1:100. --ignore-safety-checks SKIPS THE SAMPLE-LIST COMPARISON AND WRITES ANYWAY, so a record belonging to s1 is written under a header declaring only s0: the genotype is RELABELLED rather than dropped. A MISSING SEQUENCE DICTIONARY IS REFUSED BY THE INDEXER and not by the validation, with a message about ##contig lines that arrives after validation has passed. AUTOMATIC picks BLOCK only when every input and the output are block compressed, and asking for BLOCK on a plain vcf is a BadInput rather than a fallback. And the output header is the first file's, whichever mode ran.

suites.title: SelectVariants' sample selection, where matching nothing selects everything
suites.why: Which genotype columns survive -sn, -se, -xl-sn and -xl-se, decided once before any record is read. THE EXPRESSIONS ARE UNANCHORED find() AND NOT matches(), so -se s1 selects xs10 as well as s1 and a list written as names reaches further than it reads. AN EXPRESSION THAT MATCHES NOTHING SELECTS EVERYTHING, because the empty accumulated set is the same emptiness as no sample requested, and --allow-nonoverlapping-command-line-samples reaches the same place: asking for one sample that does not exist and permitting it outputs THE WHOLE COHORT. THE MISSING-NAME CHECK LOOKS AT -sn ONLY and never at the expressions. THE OUTPUT ORDER IS THE SORTED ORDER and not the command line's, since both the header set and the accumulated set are TreeSets. EXCLUSION TAKES PRECEDENCE OVER INCLUSION and an emptied set is a UserException rather than an empty output, which excluding every sample reaches as well. The missing-name refusal is a four-paragraph BadInput listing the names in the order they were given, and an uncompilable expression is the regex engine's own PatternSyntaxException rather than a UserException.

suites.title: java.util.regex as GATK asks it, compile and find()
suites.why: What `-se`, `-xl-se` and ClipReads' `-X` compile, and what they then call: find(), a SEARCH, which is why `-se s1` selects a sample named `xs10`. `$` MATCHES BEFORE A FINAL LINE TERMINATOR and takes a trailing CRLF as one. `.` REFUSES FOUR LINE TERMINATORS and not one. THE PREDEFINED CLASSES ARE ASCII without UNICODE_CHARACTER_CLASS, so an Arabic-Indic digit is not a digit and an accented letter is not a word character. POSSESSIVE QUANTIFIERS TAKE AND NEVER GIVE BACK, so `^.*+1$` fails where `^.*1$` succeeds. Matching backtracks and alternation prefers the branch written first. A class whose first character is `]` contains it. AND A COMPILE FAILURE CARRIES A DESCRIPTION AND AN INDEX that reach the user unwrapped, with the index not always where a reader would put it: `a)` reports 0 and a trailing backslash reports 1, so the invalid patterns vary their prefix to pin the rule rather than one example of it.

compile	)	error	Unmatched closing ')'	-1	Unmatched closing ')'\n)
compile	a{2,1}	error	Illegal repetition range	5	Illegal repetition range near index 5\na{2,1}\n     ^

The patterns cover what a sample expression is, the constructs a subset may leave out, and thirty-four invalid or awkward ones whose prefix is varied so each rule is measured rather than guessed. An unclosed class reports the bracket, an unclosed group the character after it, an unmatched `)` the one BEFORE it (so a bare `)` reports -1 and gets no caret line at all), a bad repetition range the closing brace, a count that is not a count the character after the brace, and a trailing backslash the end, where the caret is again omitted. `{2}` with nothing before it COMPILES and matches everywhere, because the brace quantifies the empty atom. suites.title: SelectVariants subsetting a record, where the INFO DP is replaced by a sum
suites.why: What subsetGenotypesBySampleNames and addAnnotations do once the sample list is known. THE INFO DP IS RECOMPUTED FROM THE KEPT GENOTYPES AND OVERWRITES THE RECORD'S OWN, summing only the UNFILTERED ones, and it is written only where some kept genotype had a DP at all, so the same argument either replaces the field or leaves it depending on the FORMAT column. AC, AF and AN are recomputed from the kept genotypes, AC being a list for several alternates and a scalar for one. AF IS A DOUBLE THE WRITER FORMATS, so 0.5 comes out 0.500 and 0.0 comes out 0.00 in the same column. MLEAC and MLEAF are STRIPPED whenever the record is rewritten while AC and AF are replaced. --remove-unused-alternates drops an alternate nobody calls and rewrites PL and AD through AlleleSubsettingUtils, and the result is TRIMMED unless --preserve-alleles, so dropping an alternate can respell every remaining allele. --keep-original-ac writes AC_Orig, AF_Orig and AN_Orig from the input's own attributes rather than from a recount, reordering the per-allele ones when the allele list changed. And a record is returned untouched when nothing was selected and no alternate was removed.

suites.title: SelectVariants' record filters, where one fraction is an integer division
suites.why: Which records survive, decided in three places that are not interchangeable: a first round before anything is subset, two genotype-count gates in the middle, and --exclude-non-variants after the subset, with the JEXL expressions on either side depending on one flag. THE FILTERED-GENOTYPE FRACTION IS AN INTEGER DIVISION: numFilteredSamples / samples.size() is int over int assigned to a double, so --max-fraction-filtered-genotypes does nothing at any value above 0, while --max-nocall-fraction one line below casts and works. --select-type-to-exclude BEATS --select-type-to-include. The indel size gates are about ABSOLUTE length and reject the RECORD rather than the allele. --exclude-non-variants runs AFTER the subset, so it drops a record whose alternates only the unselected samples carried, and a spanning deletion alone counts as non-variant. The JEXL expressions are OR-ed and --invert-select inverts EACH of them before the or, which is not the complement of the whole; --apply-jexl-filters-first moves them before the subset, so an expression over AC sees the record's own annotation rather than the recomputed one. An expression over a per-allele annotation is a UserException at evaluation rather than a compile failure, and an unparseable one is an IllegalArgumentException whose message runs the argument name into the next word.

suites.title: SelectVariants' output order, where trimming moves a record right
suites.why: Records do not go straight to the writer: they go into a PriorityQueue ordered by start, drained only as far as the record being read, because TRIMMING CAN MOVE A RECORD RIGHT and a file written in input order would be unsorted. The queue is drained with `<=`, so a pending record at the same start as the record being read is written FIRST, and a contig change drains it entirely. Trimming only happens on the subsetting path, so adding one -sn both shortens the alleles and reorders the file. --set-filtered-gt-to-nocall replaces the call and KEEPS the FT, and recomputes AC, AN and AF itself when it replaced something, so a whole-cohort run that recomputes nothing else still rewrites the counts of that record and adds an AF the input never had. --drop-info-annotation removes a field the tool itself would have written, and --drop-genotype-annotation rebuilds every genotype through noAttributes, dropping the named key and keeping GT, GQ, DP, AD and PL, which are not extended attributes.

suites.title: SelectVariants' discordance and concordance, which are not opposites
suites.why: Both flags compare the record being read against a second VCF, and both change meaning entirely depending on whether any sample was named. WITHOUT -sn, --discordance IS ONLY 'the other file has nothing here' and --concordance ONLY 'the other file has something here': the genotypes are never looked at. WITH -sn they compare ALLELE SETS rather than genotypes, because haveSameGenotypes asks each list to contain the other, so 0/1 and 1/0 are the same call and so are 1/1 and a haploid 1. A FILTERED GENOTYPE NEVER MATCHES ANYTHING, INCLUDING ANOTHER FILTERED ONE, because haveSameGenotypes tests `g1.isCalled() && g2.isFiltered()` first and isCalled() is about alleles rather than filters: its third clause about two filtered genotypes is dead code, and --exclude-filtered moves no record in either direction for the same reason. Discordance skips hom-ref genotypes entirely; concordance requires EVERY selected sample to match. They are not negations of one another.

suites.title: VariantsToTable, where every column is a decision
suites.why: A VCF in and a tab-separated table out, where almost no column is a copy. NO FIELDS AT ALL MEANS EVERY FIELD THE HEADER DECLARES, and asking for no genotype field EMPTIES THE SAMPLE LIST. A missing field is the string NA rather than an empty cell, unless --error-if-missing-data turns it into a UserException. A field ending in `*` is a wildcard over the INFO keys joined in SORTED order. QUAL is Double.toString of the phred score, so an integer quality comes out 50.0, and FILTER is PASS for a record whose column said `.`. --split-multi-allelic produces one row per alternate and spreads a value across them ONLY when it is a list of exactly the right length, so a Number=R field lands whole in every row while a Number=A field is split; -ASF subsets an R-type field by dropping its first entry, and -ASGF AD is special-cased to a reference-and-alternate pair per row. --moltenize replaces the table with four columns and one line per value. Two of its cells carry Java's own rendering: the wildcard sorts the VALUES rather than the keys and joins a list as `[10, 5]`, brackets and space included, while -ASF strips the brackets and leaves the SPACE, so a split R-type column reads ` 5` with a leading blank.

Asking for REF without a reference is a MissingReference refusal thrown before any record is read. suites.title: CountVariants, whose count is the traversal's
suites.why: The tool's own body is three lines, so what is measured is the traversal on one side of it and the output collection on the other. THE COUNT REACHES NO STREAM WITHOUT -O: the class documentation says it prints to standard output and OptionalTextOutputArgumentCollection.print writes nothing at all when output is null, so the number survives only as the traversal's return value and the engine's log line. THE FILE HAS NO TRAILING NEWLINE, because onTraversalSuccess calls print rather than println, and it is TRUNCATED RATHER THAN APPENDED, because Files.write with no options is CREATE, TRUNCATE_EXISTING and WRITE: a count of 5 over a ten-byte file leaves one byte. EVERY ROW COUNTS, filtered or not, symbolic or not, and a second record at a position already seen counts again. A RECORD IS SELECTED BY ITS WHOLE SPAN AND NOT BY ITS POSITION, since the interval traversal is a Tribble query and the decoded stop comes from END or from the length of REF: a record at chr1:100 with END=400 is counted by -L chr1:300-310. A record spanning two intervals is still counted once, which is FeatureIntervalIterator's one-interval memory. The two refusals come from opposite ends of the run: -L without an index is thrown before any record is read, and -O onto a directory after the whole traversal, AND THAT SECOND MESSAGE IS THE PATH ALONE, because new CouldNotCreateOutputFile(output.toString(), e) selects the (String message, Exception e) overload and the IOException never reaches the text.

suites.title: CountFalsePositives, where everything that is not an indel is a SNP
suites.why: Two counters, a denominator and a six-column table, and each hides a decision. EVERYTHING THAT IS NOT AN INDEL IS A SNP: apply is `if (variant.isIndel()) indel++ else snp++` and isIndel() is getType() == INDEL and nothing looser, so an MNP, a symbolic allele, a mixed record and a record with no alternate at all land in the snp column, which is therefore not what its name says. THE ID IS A FILE NAME rather than a sample, GATKPath.getBaseName() stripping ONE extension, so a name carrying two keeps the first. THE TERRITORY IS THE MERGED INTERVALS in bases, so two overlapping -L arguments contribute their union once and 1-100 with 900-1000 is 201. THE RATES ARE PER MEGABASE AND DIVIDED BEFORE THEY ARE SCALED, count / territory * 1e6, written through DataLine.set(double) whose rounding branch is dead, so an integral rate keeps its .0 and 1 over 201 bases is 4975.124378109453. The two refusals come from opposite ends: requiresIntervals() makes -L a required argument, so its absence is Barclay's MissingArgument before the tool is built, while an output that cannot be opened is a plain UserException after the whole traversal, saying only that it encountered an IO exception while opening it.

suites.title: EvaluateInfoFieldConcordance, whose standard deviation can be NaN by arithmetic
suites.why: The first tool written on the concordance iterator: for every true positive it takes the difference between one INFO field of each side and reports a mean and a standard deviation per variant type. A RECORD WHOSE KEY IS ABSENT IS COUNTED BUT CONTRIBUTES NOTHING, the counter being incremented in apply and the delta only inside infoDifference, which returns early unless BOTH records carry their key: the baseline's four deltas of 1.0 over five counted true positives report 0.8. THE STANDARD DEVIATION CAN BE NaN BY ARITHMETIC ALONE, the variance being the cancelling form (sumSq - sum * sum / n) / n with no guard, so equal deltas can land just below zero and the square root of that is NaN. AN EMPTY BUCKET IS TWO NaN COLUMNS, n = 0 making both 0/0, so a run with no indel among its true positives still writes an INDEL row and that row is NaN NaN, and a run where nothing agrees writes two of them. The mean is of absolute differences computed as sqrt(delta * delta) rather than abs(delta), which is not the same function of a double in general. Only true positives are looked at, and this walker drops filtered records on both sides, so two of the iterator's five states cannot occur. A key either header does not declare is a UserException before any record, worded with the file it was not found in.

suites.title: Concordance's summary table, where an empty callset's recall is zero rather than NaN
suites.why: The tool the concordance iterator was written for, measured on its --summary table alone: five states tallied into six columns, one row for SNPs and one for everything else. AN EMPTY CALLSET REPORTS ZERO RATHER THAN NaN, both rates being long divisions printed through MathUtils.roundToNDecimalPlaces(x, 3), which is Math.round((x + ulp(x)) * 1000) / 1000, and Math.round of NaN is 0: the same 0/0 that EvaluateInfoFieldConcordance writes as NaN is written here as 0.0. A FILTERED EVAL RECORD ALONE LEAVES NO TRACE, FILTERED_TRUE_NEGATIVE being counted into the enum map and never read, while the FN column is FALSE_NEGATIVE + FILTERED_FALSE_NEGATIVE, so an unmatched filtered record moves neither rate and a filtered one at a truth locus counts as a miss without counting as a false positive. THE TRUTH SIDE DROPS SYMBOLIC AND SV RECORDS AND THE EVAL SIDE KEEPS EVERYTHING, so the same symbolic record in both files is a false positive rather than a true positive. AGREEMENT NEEDS THE SAME NUMBER OF ALTERNATES BUT ONLY TRUTH'S FIRST, so A/C against A/C,G disagrees on the count while A/C,G against A/G,C agrees. And the rounding is half-up after an ulp is added, so 2/3 prints 0.667.

suites.title: ApplyVQSR's per-record filtering, where the last tranche means PASS
suites.why: ApplyVQSR's per-record half, measured on an input VCF of eight records against a recal VCF and the three-tranche file of the apply-vqsr-tranches suite. THE TRANCHES ARE WALKED BACKWARDS AND THE LAST ONE MEANS PASS: the loop takes the first tranche whose minVQSLod the record reaches and answers PASS only when that tranche is the last of the reversed list, so the bands are exactly the intervals the FILTER header lines describe, a LOD equal to a minVQSLod belongs to the tranche below it, and anything under every tranche gets the FIRST tranche's name with a + appended. THE RECAL RECORD MUST AGREE ON BOTH ENDS, BY TWO DIFFERENT MECHANISMS: the query is getValues(recal, vc.getStart()), which keeps only records STARTING at the input record's start, and getMatchingRecalVC then takes the first of those whose END matches, so a recal record at the same start with another length is skipped and one with no partner at all is a refusal. EVERY NEGATIVE VQSLOD IS WRITTEN IN SCIENTIFIC NOTATION: the value is reparsed as a double and handed to htsjdk's formatVCFDouble, whose branch is on the SIGNED value, so -3.0 comes out -3.000e+00 while 5.0 comes out 5.00 and 0.0 comes out 0.00. A RECAL RECORD WITH NO CULPRIT WRITES culprit=. , the attribute being copied with getAttribute and no default. A RECORD OF THE WRONG CLASS OR ONE ALREADY FILTERED IS EMITTED UNTOUCHED, and --exclude-filtered NEVER DROPS IT: the exclusion is inside the branch that recalibrates, so an already-filtered record survives a run that drops every record the tool itself filtered. --ignore-all-filters and --ignore-filter each bring it back into the recalibration. AND THE THREE REFUSALS ARE WRAPPED: what apply throws is a UserException, and the walker rethrows it as a GATKException whose message is the locus and the whole VariantContext, so the tool's own wording survives only in the cause.

suites.title: ApplyVQSR run twice, where the leniency regex loses a digit
suites.why: ApplyVQSR run twice over the same records, which is how a mixed site is filtered at all: the second run reads the first run's own FILTER lines back out of the header and then compares the two modes' filter names. THE PREVIOUS RUN IS DETECTED BY THREE MAGIC NUMBERS: a FILTER ID of at least 12 characters whose first 11 are VQSRTranche ignoring case and whose 12th is S or I, with the interval taken as substring(14) or substring(16), the lengths of VQSRTrancheSNP and VQSRTrancheINDEL. THE PREFIX TEST IS CASE-INSENSITIVE AND THE MODE TEST IS NOT, so a header line named vqsrtranchesnp90.00to99.00 passes the first and fails the second and the run behaves as though no SNP mode had ever been applied. A NAME WHOSE INTERVAL SPLITS INTO TWO PIECES THAT ARE NOT NUMBERS IS A UserException thrown before any record, worded 'Poorly formatted tranche filter name does not contain two sensitivity interval end points.' THE SITE FILTER OF THE SECOND RUN IS THE MOST LENIENT OF BOTH MODES, and most lenient means the smallest lower limit pulled out of the filter NAME by the regex VQSRTranche\\S+(\\d+\\.\\d+)to(\\d+\\.\\d+). THAT REGEX IS GREEDY AND LOSES A DIGIT: \\S+ eats as much as it can, so VQSRTrancheINDEL90.00to99.00 has a lower limit of 0.00 rather than 90.00 while VQSRTrancheSNP5.00to90.00 keeps its 5.00, and the second run therefore filters the site with the LESS lenient of the two names. The golden runs the same pair twice, once with names the loss does not reorder and once with names it does. suites.title: FilterVariantTranches, whose cutoff is a truncated index into the resource scores
suites.why: A two-pass walker: the first pass collects the INPUT record's own score wherever it overlaps a resource, and the second turns those scores into cutoffs and filters against them. THE CUTOFF IS A TRUNCATED INDEX INTO THE RESOURCE SCORES: they are sorted DESCENDING and the index is (int)((t / 100.0) * (size - 1)), so five scores and a tranche of 50 answer index 2 and a higher tranche means a LOWER cutoff. THE SCORE STORED IS THE INPUT'S, NOT THE RESOURCE'S, and it is stored once: the loop returns on its first match, so a record overlapping two resources contributes one score. MEMBERSHIP IS DECIDED BY THE FIRST CUTOFF ALONE, score <= cutoffs.get(0), which is the smallest tranche's cutoff because the list was sorted, and the comparison is <=, so the golden's indel scoring exactly 8.0 against a cutoff of 8.0 is filtered. THE BAND IS THEN FOUND BY WALKING THE CUTOFFS, and a score below every one of them lands in the last band, which always runs to 100.00. THE TRANCHE LIST IS DEDUPLICATED AND SORTED before any of that, and refused outright unless every value is in [0, 100): a tranche of 100 is a CommandLineException, and the golden runs the same two tranches given out of order with one of them twice to show the result is identical. THE FILTER NAMES ARE BUILT WITH %.2f as <info key>_<type>_Tranche_<t1>_<t2>. A RECORD WITH NO SCORE IS STILL WRITTEN AND STILL PASSES, since passFilters() is applied to anything the tool did not filter. --invalidate-previous-filters clears the FILTER lines of the header as well as the records'. suites.title: The Mutect threshold calculator, whose optimal F score keeps the last tie
suites.why: The piece of FilterMutectCalls that decides where the error probability is cut: a list of per-variant posteriors in, one threshold out, by one of three strategies. THE LIST IS SORTED IN PLACE, so the caller's own list comes back reordered. THE OPTIMAL F SCORE KEEPS THE LAST TIE, the comparison being F >= optimalFScore rather than >, so four equal posteriors of 0.2 resolve to the last index and therefore to a threshold of 1.0. ITS ANSWER IS THREE-WAY: no index at all is 0, the last index is 1, and anything else is the posterior AT that index, so three hopeless posteriors answer 0.97 while three clean ones answer 1.0. THE FALSE DISCOVERY RATE WALKS UNTIL THE RATE IS EXCEEDED AND STEPS BACK ONE, so the threshold is the last posterior that kept the cumulative rate acceptable, 0.0 when that was the very first one and 1.0 when the rate was never exceeded. CONSTANT LEAVES THE INITIAL THRESHOLD ALONE whatever was accumulated. RELEARNING CLEARS THE ACCUMULATED PROBABILITIES, so relearning twice computes the second threshold from an empty list, and THE TWO STRATEGIES ANSWER AN EMPTY LIST DIFFERENTLY: 1.0 for the false discovery rate and 0.0 for the F score. And a negative beta or rate is refused by ParamUtils with the caller's own wording.

suites.title: The Mutect filtering stats file, whose two roundings disagree
suites.why: The .filteringStats.tsv that FilterMutectCalls writes beside its VCF, measured through FilterStats.writeM2FilterSummary directly. THE TWO ROUNDINGS DISAGREE: the columns go through DataLine.set(name, value, 2) and the metadata through roundToNDecimalPlaces(x, 3), so the same number is written to two decimals in the table and three above it. BOTH TURN NaN INTO ZERO, the rounding being Math.round((x + ulp(x)) * mult) / mult and Math.round answering 0 for NaN, so a run with no passing call divides by zero and writes 0.0 rather than NaN. BUT INFINITY BECOMES A VERY LARGE NUMBER rather than Infinity: Math.round saturates at Long.MAX_VALUE, so a false-positive count over zero calls writes fdr=9.223372036854776E15. AND A NEGATIVE ROUNDS THE OTHER WAY, since the rounding is floor(x + 0.5) after an ulp: -1.005 comes out -1.0 where 1.005 comes out 1.01, and -0.0005 comes out 0.0 with the sign gone. THE ROWS ARE THE CALLER'S, in the caller's order and unfiltered: the rule that drops a filter accounting for nothing lives in FilteringOutputStats rather than here. suites.title: Mutect's hard filters, where a long indel is judged by the reference's mapping quality
suites.why: Seven of FilterMutectCalls' filters read one INFO annotation and answer without consulting the filtering engine at all, which is what makes them measurable on their own, one VariantContext at a time. ONLY A LONG INSERTION IS JUDGED BY THE REFERENCE'S MAPPING QUALITY. MappingQualityFilter substitutes the ref annotation for any allele whose indel length reaches the long-indel size, and getIndelLengths() is the ALT length minus the REF length, which is NEGATIVE for a deletion: the golden's seven-base deletion and seven-base insertion carry the same MMQ of 60,20 and come out true and false. suites.title: Mutect's engine arithmetic, where rounding the error is a clamp
suites.why: The three public statics of Mutect2FilteringEngine that every filter goes through, measured before the engine that calls them exists. THE POSTERIOR IS A TWO-ENTRY NORMALISATION, [logOdds + logPrior, log1mexp(logPrior)] through normalizeFromLogToLinearSpace, of which the SECOND entry is returned: it is the probability of ERROR, and it falls as the odds of being real rise. A PRIOR OF ONE MAKES THE ERROR IMPOSSIBLE, log1mexp(0) being negative infinity, so every finite log odds answers 0.0 against a prior of 1. BUT THE TWO INFINITIES DO NOT AGREE: log odds of -Infinity against a prior of 1 makes both entries -Infinity and answers NaN, while log odds of +Infinity against a prior of 0 makes the sum NaN and is refused outright with 'logValues must be non-infinite and non-NAN'. roundFinitePrecisionErrors IS A CLAMP rather than a rounding, max(min(p, 1), 0): it moves 1.0000000001 to 1.0 and -Infinity to 0.0, AND IT LEAVES NaN ALONE, because Java's Math.min and Math.max propagate NaN where a naive clamp would not. AND getTumorLogOdds CONVERTS FROM LOG10 TO NATURAL LOG, so a TLOD of 6.0 is 13.815510557964275 by the time any threshold sees it, and a missing annotation is null rather than an empty array.

suites.title: The germline probability, whose answer is the first entry and not the second

suites.title: The beta-binomial Mutect's clusters are built on
suites.why: The beta-binomial likelihood every Mutect cluster is built on. BetaBinomialDistribution.logProbability is three commons-math calls, binomialCoefficientLog(n, k) + logBeta(k + alpha, n - k + beta) - logBeta(alpha, beta), and SomaticClusteringModel.logLikelihoodGivenSomatic sums it over the clusters. THE THREE PIECES ARE MEASURED SEPARATELY AS WELL AS TOGETHER, because a port has a choice at logBeta: commons-math computes it by a four-branch NSWC expansion and the obvious identity logGamma(p) + logGamma(q) - logGamma(p + q) is a different sequence of roundings. The 52 logBeta rows cross every branch boundary: min(p,q) below 1, at 1, above 2, and at or above 10. THE FLAT BETA IS THE BACKGROUND CLUSTER, alpha = beta = 1, where logBeta(1, 1) is NEGATIVE zero -- a port whose test compares with == will not notice, since -0.0 equals 0.0 -- and the beta-binomial is uniform over the counts, THOUGH NOT BIT-IDENTICALLY SO: at n = 10 the answer is -2.3978952727983707 at k = 0, ...716 at k = 1 and ...700 at k = 5, because the cancellation between the coefficient and the two beta terms is only approximate. THE HIGH-AF CLUSTER IS alpha = 10, beta = 1, whose likelihood rises from -12.126791314602453 at no alternate reads to -0.693147180559945 at ten of ten. binomialCoefficientLog ITSELF HAS FOUR BRANCHES, exact integer arithmetic below n = 67, a floating product below 1030, a symmetry fold, and a sum of logs above that. A count past the total is negative infinity by an explicit branch, and a negative count is an IllegalArgumentException.

suites.title: The power a validation pileup has
suites.why: The layer above the beta-binomial suite, which pins logProbability and stops there. THE CUMULATIVE PROBABILITY IS A PLAIN LOOP over probability(i), summed with += and not compensated, so it is not the DoubleStream.sum every other accumulation in this port has had to be. suites.title: The allele-fraction clusters, whose corrected likelihood is a Dirichlet normalisation
suites.why: The two AlleleFractionCluster implementations SomaticClusteringModel carries, on top of the beta-binomial the sibling suite pins. THE CORRECTED LOG LIKELIHOOD IS NOT A LIKELIHOOD: it is the record's TLOD corrected for the cluster's shape by four Dirichlet normalisations, g(a, b) - g(a + alt, b + ref) - g(1, 1) + g(1 + alt, 1 + ref), where g is logGamma(sum) - sum(logGamma). The original shape is always FLAT_BETA, so two of the four terms are constants -- AND THEY DO NOT CANCEL IN DOUBLES. BinomialCluster HAS NO BINOMIAL IN IT: its constructor turns a mean into a beta shape at a fixed standard-deviation-over-mean of 0.01, CLAMPING THE MEAN AT 1 - 0.01 first, so a cluster asked for a mean of one is not given one. alphaPlusBeta is ((1 - mean) / (mean * 0.0001)) - 1, enormous at a small mean, which is what drives logBeta into its a >= 10 branch. Datum's non-sequencing-error probability is a COMBINATION computed in the constructor, 1 - (1 - artifactProb) * (1 - nonSomaticProb), and the datum keeps no field for the second input. suites.title: The EM iteration and the quantile initialisation the clustering model learns by
suites.why: What learnAndClearAccumulatedData does with the data record collected, and the two learn methods under it. BetaBinomialCluster.learn IS GRADIENT ASCENT WITH FLOORS: ten epochs over the data at a rate of 0.01, each step Math.max(alpha + rate * gradient * responsibility, 1.0) and the same for beta at 0.5, and THE FLOOR IS APPLIED EVERY STEP rather than at the end, so a shape that would have dipped below it and come back cannot. suites.title: Applying the filters, where SITE is a placeholder and a filter can fire without being named
suites.why: Mutect2FilteringEngine.applyFiltersAndAccumulateOutputStats, the step that turns a record's per-filter probabilities into the FILTER column and the AS_FilterStatus annotation. The engine's filter list is replaced by reflection with filters whose name, type, arity and probabilities the dump chooses outright, so the input to the step is exact; FilteringOutputStats counts by filter OBJECT and its map is built at construction, so it is rebuilt over the replaced list. A FILTER CAN FIRE WITHOUT BEING NAMED IN THE FILTER COLUMN: only entries reaching min(maxErrorProb, MIN_REPORTABLE_ERROR_PROBABILITY = 0.1) are written, and the comment beside it says this will not change whether a variant is filtered -- it changes which names appear. SITE IS A PLACEHOLDER, NOT A FILTER, removed when an allele has any real filter and added back when it has none. A SITE-LEVEL FILTER IS DERIVED FROM THE ALLELE-LEVEL ONES ONLY WHEN EVERY ALLELE AGREES. FAIL IS THE SITE'S ANSWER WHEN EVERY ALLELE IS FILTERED FOR A DIFFERENT REASON, and only when no site filter has already been recorded. THE PHRED-SCALED ANNOTATION IS WRITTEN ONLY WHEN THE FILTER'S REQUIRED ANNOTATIONS ARE PRESENT, and it is written even when the filter did not fire. WHAT THE RUN ADDED, and it is a defect rather than a subtlety: THE SYMBOLIC-ALLELE REMOVAL IS APPLIED TWICE. suites.title: What a non-final pass records, and the record it skips
suites.why: Mutect2FilteringEngine.accumulateData and the pass schedule FilterMutectCalls drives it with: the last computation between the ported filters and an end-to-end run. THE TOOL TRAVERSES THE VCF FOUR TIMES, NOT TWO. numberOfPasses() is NUMBER_OF_LEARNING_PASSES + 2. Passes 0, 1 and 2 all accumulate; only 0 and 1 learn parameters afterwards. suites.title: The eighteen filters over one record, and what the engine makes of their answers
suites.why: The whole filtering engine over one record: every filter's answer in construction order, the per-type maxima, the combined probability, and what applyFilters makes of them. suites.title: The germline filter's wrapper, the last unported filter body
suites.why: GermlineFilter.calculateErrorProbability and the two helpers it calls. TWO EARLY RETURNS BRACKET THE POPULATION FREQUENCY: below 1e-10 the answer is 0 and above 1 - 1e-10 it is 1, the frequency being Math.pow(10, -POPAF[maxLodIndex]), so a POPAF of 0 means an allele fixed in the population and answers a hard one. maxLodIndex IS CHOSEN FROM TLOD AND THEN INDEXES THREE ARRAYS with three conventions: POPAF per alternate, the depth array with + 1, and the weighted allele fractions per alternate. suites.title: The three PairHMM implementations over the same pairs, before either is ported
suites.why: HaplotypeCaller picks FASTEST_AVAILABLE, which resolves to VectorLoglessPairHMM -- Intel GKL, AVX, through JNI -- whenever the native library loads. suites.title: The decomposition CalculateContamination waits on, and what it is used for
suites.why: SingularValueDecomposition on the matrices KernelSegmenter builds, and the changepoints it turns them into. CalculateContamination is blocked on this decomposition and nothing else, and what has to be decided before a line is ported is whether byte identity is required THROUGH the decomposition or only through what the segmenter does with it. THE SUBSAMPLE IS SEEDED, new Random(1216) through RandomGeneratorFactory, so the matrix is deterministic and a port that subsampled differently would decompose a different matrix. THE SINGULAR VALUES ARE USED AS 1 / (sqrt(s) + 1e-10), so a small one is amplified. U'S SIGN CONVENTION REACHES THE OUTPUT, the reduced matrix multiplying by U column by column. AND THE CHANGEPOINTS ARE INDICES, so they can agree while the arithmetic under them does not. WHAT THE RUN ADDED, AND IT DECIDES THE QUESTION: THE KERNEL MATRIX IS RANK-DEFICIENT AND THE NULL SPACE IS AMPLIFIED. The two-step series gives singular values 4.43, 1.0, 0.57, 1.65e-17 and two exact zeros; the flat series gives 6.0 and five exact zeros. A zero singular value goes through 1 / (0 + 1e-10) = 1e10, so the U columns that span the null space -- which are NOT determined by the matrix, any orthonormal basis of it being as valid as any other -- are multiplied by ten billion and dominate the reduced observation matrix. Byte identity through this decomposition is therefore not merely hard: in the null space the reference's own U is an artefact of its bidiagonalisation order rather than a property of the input, and a conforming implementation is free to answer differently. What can be compared is the changepoints, and the golden holds those too: 29 and 59 for the two-step series, none for the flat one, five for the ramp, and none again when the penalty is raised.

The dimension is small on purpose: the question is which bits differ, not how many there are. suites.title: The contamination model and the tool around it
suites.why: CalculateContamination is the last unblocked member of the reporting-walker archetype and the decomposition under it is already ported and pinned by kernel-segmentation. This measures everything above it. THE COVERAGE FILTER USES A MEDIAN AND A MEAN, the low threshold a ratio of the median and the high threshold a ratio of the mean, both computed after dropping sites at or below MIN_COVERAGE. THE MODEL ITERATES THREE TIMES between minor allele fractions and contamination, feeding the previous contamination back in, so a port that solved once lands somewhere else. THE LOH SEARCH WALKS THE THRESHOLD DOWN in steps of 0.04 and stops at the first threshold keeping more than a quarter of the sites, so the answer depends on the order of the walk. THE STRATEGY CASCADE IS THREE STRATEGIES OVER ONE LOOP, hom alt above 0.25, hom ref down to 0.20, then the unscrupulous hom ref, returning the first estimate whose standard error is small enough relative to the estimate. THE STANDARD ERROR IS A BINARY SEARCH and the closed formula is only its fallback. THE UNSCRUPULOUS STRATEGY GOES THROUGH A PERCENTILE, so its threshold is commons-math's interpolation rather than a sorted index. AND THE SEGMENTATION IS PER CONTIG, so a contig with too few het sites for the window is one segment rather than none. The sites are built from a formula with integer counts so a port rebuilds exactly the same input.

suites.title: What a validation pileup says about an allele
suites.why: Everything ValidateBasicSomaticShortMutations does before the arithmetic somatic-validation-power already pins. typeOfVariant CALLS EQUAL-LENGTH ALLELES DIFFERING IN ONE BASE A SNP however long they are, and calls a spanning-deletion alternate NO_VARIATION. isComplexIndel IS A PREFIX TEST, so a deletion whose remaining base disagrees with the reference's first is complex and its genotype cannot be validated at all. chooseAlleleForRead DOES NOT STOP AT THE FIRST MATCH, so the last matching alternate wins. THE REFERENCE TEST INCLUDES THE INDEL LOOKAHEAD, so a read whose bases match the reference is still not reference when it precedes an insertion or a deletion. A READ THAT ENDS INSIDE THE ALLELE ANSWERS UNKNOWN rather than false and is neither reference nor alternate. THE QUALITY CUTOFF IS APPLIED LAST, to the chosen allele's own bases, and the minimum over an empty array is minus one. THE DELETION MATCH COMPARES LENGTHS ONLY, so an alternate of the right length matches whatever its bases are. AllelePileupCounter DROPS MAPPING QUALITY 0 AND 255 and drops nothing else. calculateMaxAltRatio's TWO FILTERS ARE NOT COMPLEMENTS, so a pileup of nothing but short reads is a ratio of zero rather than a NaN. suites.title: The validation table a tool writes
suites.why: The walker over the counting allele-pileup-counter pins and the arithmetic somatic-validation-power pins.
